unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_2
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Purpose, design philosophy and framework boundary

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: CakeUI (CUI) is the authoritative 9to1 user-interface framework and .cui is the only final application-markup format for first-party 9to1 applications. CUI is intentionally small, opinionated and quick to learn: ordinary application authors work with a fixed compact element vocabulary, Types, properties, Themes, Definitions, Prefabs, variables, Styles/actions and a small set of structural language constructs rather than an Avalonia-sized public control taxonomy.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Page — root navigation/render surface and top-level UI scope.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Container — general layout/composition element; layout behaviour is selected primarily through Type and properties.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Object — host for specialised renderers/objects such as graphs, Canvas surfaces, browser/media/document engines and other non-primitive content.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Input — standard input family; Type selects text, number, checkbox, slider and other registered input behaviours.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Layer — rendering-depth container; Layer is also available as an element property.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Theme, Style, Property, Variable, Prefab, ActionEvent/&, If, Else, Repeat, Import and Keyframe/@.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Built-in language/framework keywords are case-insensitive. User-defined IDs, Groups, C# variables, custom Definition names, Prefab IDs and other user symbols are case-sensitive unless the owning external language/package explicitly defines different rules.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: CUI uses XML-like nesting but is its own strict language. Most behavioural variation is expressed through Type and properties rather than different primitive element names.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Attribute-assignment shorthand uses a colon after an identifier. The following are equivalent when unambiguous:

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: For unquoted shorthand values, underscore MAY represent a space. Therefore Type:Vertical_Stack resolves to Type="Vertical Stack" when that is the only valid symbol. Quoted values are literal and underscore substitution never occurs inside quotes.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Comments use <# and #> and MAY span multiple lines. Comments do not nest and do not create runtime nodes.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Formatting whitespace outside text-bearing content is ignored. Text content uses the Text element's whitespace policy; the default collapses source indentation/newline whitespace that exists only for readable markup, while Whitespace:Preserve retains exact authored whitespace.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: (Definition) is a declaration modifier. A Definition creates reusable language/component definitions and is not rendered merely because its declaration is present.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The declaration above creates a reusable Paragraph element that can later be instantiated as <Paragraph>...</Paragraph>.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Theme is an inherited visual-design scope. Everything within a Theme uses that Theme until a descendant Theme overrides it; after the descendant closes, inheritance returns to the parent Theme.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Users can define custom Theme types in .cui-theme files.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Static Prefab — all live instances share one internal mutable Prefab state. If an internal property/state changes, every live instance reflects the same shared state. Host placement, host parent, host size and host Active state remain per instance.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dynamic Prefab — each instance receives independent runtime state while sharing the same compiled implementation/defaults.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Static Prefab state is runtime-shared, not automatically persistent across process restart. Persistence occurs only when the owning Prefab/app explicitly stores that state.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Prefab inputs are declared using Variable Definitions or another equivalent typed public-definition form implemented by the compiler.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Ordinary application variables remain ordinary implementation-language values. CUI reactivity is attached to the CUI reference by default; application authors do not have to wrap every value in a special Live<T> type merely to update UI.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: <:Name:> is the compact live variable-reference form. Live is assumed unless static is explicitly requested.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Typed/conversion shorthand prefixes the target type:

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The long conversion forms are equivalent:

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A live CUI reference subscribes to the referenced CUI-visible value and automatically reevaluates the dependent UI when that value changes. A static CUI reference evaluates on load/explicit refresh and does not update merely because the source changes.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Static subexpressions retain their last evaluated value even when another live reference in the same element causes an unrelated update. Element.Refresh() explicitly reevaluates the element's static references; refreshing a Container/Page recursively refreshes the applicable active subtree.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: new Live(...) is reserved for relationships between application values/objects, not for basic CUI binding.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: ID and Name are aliases for the same unique identity mechanism. An element may own zero or one ID/Name and any number of Groups. Multiple elements may belong to the same Group.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: ID shorthand is :: and Group shorthand is :::.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Generated/runtime handles allow direct element mutation:

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Groups are dynamic: active or inactive members remain members while the corresponding object exists. Persistent active Styles targeting a Group apply to newly loaded compatible members while that Style remains active.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Properties are strongly typed registered CUI properties. The long Property form and compact $ form are semantically equivalent.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The short closing form </$> closes the most recently opened property region when nesting is unambiguous.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A property region is a typed property scope, not an ordinary visual element. It can have an ID or Groups using the same shorthand system.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Multiple property declarations may contribute different property types to the same Group. If a target Group exposes exactly one property type, a property mutation may omit the property name. If multiple property types are available, the property name is mandatory.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: CUI markup may mutate an existing property target/Group declaratively.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Outside a Style/event rule, a mutation directive executes when its containing declaration becomes active/loaded and executes again on later reactivation. It is a persistent stored-property mutation, not an automatically reversible Style overlay.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Text and Children are distinct runtime surfaces.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Text is literal textual content. Assigning markup-looking characters to Text displays them as text.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Children is structured CUI child content. Assigning to Children parses the value as a CUI child fragment under the host's allowed component/action capabilities.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Assignment means Replace by default; Replace() is the explicit equivalent and Add() appends.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Active=True means the element/declaration participates in its normal active lifecycle/tree. Active=False deactivates/unloads it from normal layout/render/input participation while retaining enough object/state information for later reactivation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Hidden=True suppresses visual rendering only. A hidden active object still occupies layout, retains state and can receive interaction/events when Interactive=True.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Interactive=False disables user-originated interaction/focus targeting while leaving the active object visible/layout-participating unless another property changes that.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: All objects default to Active=True, Hidden=False and Interactive=True unless a Definition/Type/Theme explicitly defines another default.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Normal descendants inherit Active state from the nearest active parent. Effective Active is Self.Active AND parent EffectiveActive.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A leading ! or ActiveIndependently=True breaks only the parent-to-child Active dependency.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Initial activation generates Loaded. A False-to-True Active transition generates Loaded again. A True-to-False transition generates Deactivated. Event processing is typed and follows the ActionEvent rules below.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Stateful/non-once events are temporary overlays for the event lifetime; Once-prefixed variants commit their property/action result as persistent state rather than reverting with event end. Once means committed/persistent, not 'execute only once ever'.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Width, Height, MinWidth, MaxWidth, MinHeight and MaxHeight.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: HorizontalAlignment, VerticalAlignment, wrapping/overflow and scrolling properties.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Grid Rows, Columns, RowSizes, ColumnSizes, Row, Column, RowSpan and ColumnSpan.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Absolute X/Y positioning and associated coordinate modes.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Typography, colour, background, borders, corner radii, opacity, clipping, transforms, shadows/effects and other applicable mature property families.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Container Type:Grid performs row/column layout. Container Type:Vertical_Stack and Horizontal_Stack perform ordered stack layout. CellGap controls spacing between grid/stack cells/items; CellMargin controls the per-cell/item margin contribution.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Scrolling is orthogonal to layout Type and can be enabled independently.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Container Type:Absolute enables free child positioning. Bare X and Y use CUI's proportional coordinate system by default and MAY be decimal values.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The centre of the positioning surface is (0,0). The normal horizontal range is -1000 at the left edge to +1000 at the right edge. The normal vertical range is -1000 at the bottom edge to +1000 at the top edge. Values outside the normal range are legal and place the reference point beyond the surface, which is useful for transitions/off-screen UI.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: An axis may alternatively use X-px/Y-px for CUI logical pixels or X-%/Y-% for percentage positioning. Percentage 0 is left/bottom, 50 is centre and 100 is right/top. Coordinates in every mode MAY be decimals.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: An element may define only one authoritative positioning mode per axis at a time. Supplying X and X-px together, for example, is an error.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: X-Inherited and Y-Inherited independently recalibrate descendant coordinate resolution to the declaring Container's bounds.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: X-Inherited=True makes that Container's left/right bounds the descendant -1000/+1000 X range and the corresponding percentage/pixel reference surface.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Y-Inherited=True makes that Container's bottom/top bounds the descendant -1000/+1000 Y range and the corresponding percentage/pixel reference surface.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The nearest applicable inherited axis scope wins. X and Y may therefore resolve against different ancestor Containers. Outside an Absolute/free-positioning context, free X/Y placement is invalid unless the owning specialised Type explicitly declares support.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Layer is both a container element and an inheritable signed-integer property.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Higher Layer values render/hit-test above lower values; negative and positive values are valid. An element-level Layer overrides the parent layer and becomes the inherited layer for its normal descendants unless they override it again. Equal layers use normal tree/source order, with the later item above the earlier item where they overlap.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Layer controls depth only; it does not by itself imply modal behaviour or layout.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Modal is a separate property. Modal=True traps applicable focus/input inside the modal subtree and blocks lower-layer interaction in the same render surface until dismissal. Nonmodal high-layer popups may sit above content without blocking unrelated lower-layer interaction outside their bounds.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Anchor is an optional named placement point, not a prerequisite for loading a Prefab or dynamically created UI.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: LoadAt(x,y) — fixed proportional coordinates in the selected/current Absolute coordinate scope.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Relative placement operations such as LoadUnder, LoadAbove, LoadAt(anchor) and LoadIn(grid,...) remain live placement relationships and track target movement/resizing. Raw coordinate placement is fixed in the chosen coordinate scope unless the caller changes it.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: When multiple Prefabs/UI instances are loaded at the same Anchor without another placement rule, they flow downward from that Anchor in load order. Raw repeated coordinate loads overlap unless another rule is supplied.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A direct runtime property assignment changes the stored explicit property value at its normal level; it is not an invisible new top-level precedence layer. If a temporary event Style currently overrides that property, the new stored value becomes visible when the temporary overlay ends.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Action events use the long form <ActionEvent Type="..."> or & shorthand.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Inside a Style, an ActionEvent begins a rule and following property/action declarations belong to that event until the next ActionEvent or the end of the Style. A property declaration before any event is an unconditional Style property while that Style is active.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Curly braces declare an explicit target. {::foo} targets ID foo; {:::foo} targets Group foo. TargetID and TargetGroup are the verbose equivalent attributes.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: When an event/property declaration is owned by an element/Style and no explicit target is provided, it targets the owning element/context according to that construct's standard rule.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Stateful events such as Hover apply their associated Style overlay only while the state is active; ending Hover automatically reveals the previously effective values. OnceHover commits the resulting mutation so it remains after Hover ends.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The same temporary-versus-committed distinction applies to corresponding event families such as Clicked/OnceClick, Loaded/OnceLoaded and Deactivated/OnceDeactivated where meaningful. Once-prefixed events may execute on later qualifying occurrences; 'Once' denotes committed effect semantics, not a one-time lifetime subscription.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Events target the actual originating element by default and do not automatically bubble through every parent. Bubble=True enables supported upward propagation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Event.Cancel() cancels further compatible propagation/action when the event family permits cancellation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Displaying a variable is one-way by default. Writable Input properties bind two-way by default when the source is writable and the conversion is valid.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: WriteBack=False disables automatic source update. A :static reference is snapshot-only and has no automatic write-back.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: When typed conversion fails during input, the control retains the invalid entered representation and exposes validation error state; the source variable is not overwritten until conversion succeeds.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Condition is live by default. When the condition changes, the applicable branch is instantiated and the other branch is removed from the structural tree. A static condition reevaluates only on explicit containing-scope refresh.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Structural removal is stronger than Active inheritance: an ActiveIndependently child cannot remain alive after the entire conditional branch that owns it ceases to exist.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: At minimum, applicable registered properties include:

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Rotate, Scale, ScaleX, ScaleY, Skew, SkewX, SkewY, Translate, TranslateX and TranslateY.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Opacity, Background, Foreground/Color, Border, BorderColor, BorderWidth, CornerRadius, Shadow, Clip and Effect.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Typography, text alignment/wrapping, layout sizing/alignment, scrolling, cursor/input/focus and accessibility properties.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Properties remain strongly typed. Unknown/incompatible property names or values are compiler errors when statically knowable.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Effect and Background modifier chains have different targets.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Effect processes the element's own rendered appearance. Effect:Blur(1), for example, blurs that element.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A fully transparent background exposes the processed backdrop directly; a semi-transparent colour/material composites over the processed backdrop; a fully opaque result may make the backdrop invisible and may be optimised away when observationally equivalent.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_2
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Blur, Refract and chained backdrop modifiers

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Blur uses a ratio by default: Blur(1) is equivalent to Blur(100%), Blur(0.5) to Blur(50%). The renderer maps the public ratio to the platform blur implementation deterministically.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Refract is a built-in live backdrop modifier that refracts/distorts content behind the Background, enabling liquid-glass-like materials.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Backdrop modifiers are evaluated left-to-right. Visual properties with a defined backdrop-rendering interpretation may participate as modifiers. For example:

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Gradient is a first-class property value/modifier.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Animation is the canonical property used to apply a named animation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Named animations are declared using @ shorthand or Keyframe long form.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Keyframe positions may be percentages or absolute time in milliseconds.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: <$1000> means 1000 milliseconds / one second. Explicit ms/s duration syntax is also supported. Percentage keyframes require a declared/inferable Animation duration; absolute-time keyframes may infer total duration from the greatest absolute keyframe when no longer Duration is declared.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Keyframe bodies contain ordinary typed property declarations. Animatable/interpolatable property types interpolate between frames; non-interpolatable properties switch at the relevant frame boundary.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Assigning/changing Animation while an element is active starts/restarts it according to its playback properties. An animation applied by a temporary Style follows that Style's lifetime unless its action explicitly commits/persists animation state.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The CUI toolchain automatically indexes supported local .cui, .cui-theme and .cui-prefab files within the declared project/source roots. External/shared packages use Import.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: First-party compiled .cui, Plugin CUI and Generative UI are different trust classes.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Compiled first-party CUI may reference its declared application contracts.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Plugin/external CUI surfaces execute inside their declared/authorised host capability environment and do not gain action permissions merely by rendering controls.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Static syntax/type/property/binding errors are build/compile errors with file, line and column diagnostics and, where safe, suggested corrections.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Hot reload preserves the current valid runtime tree when edited CUI is invalid. Once valid again, compatible nodes are patched while preserving state by stable IDs where unambiguous. Definition/Theme/Prefab changes update compatible live instances without arbitrarily resetting unrelated runtime state.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Live variable changes invalidate only dependent expressions/properties/subtrees.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Performance acceptance requires measured evidence on the declared supported-hardware/platform baseline. 'Looks fast' is not sufficient.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Native CUI applications depend on the compatible Home-managed CUI/shared runtime under the global Home runtime-dependency contract. The CUI compiler/toolchain belongs to the development/build environment; the runtime version/capability requirement is recorded in app/package metadata.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The canonical pipeline is parse -> shorthand normalization -> symbol/import resolution -> Definition/Prefab/Theme expansion metadata -> typed property/variable/action validation -> accessibility/static lint -> dependency graph generation -> compiled CUI representation/source maps -> runtime binding.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Chat remains in Spaces. The Dashboard MAY expose a lightweight ask/action affordance, but its primary purpose is synthesis, prioritisation, status and quick action.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: AI-generated tiles and AI layout control

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The compact picker is used inside apps, Agents and AI surfaces when selecting the effective model/route. The full manager lives in Home/Settings → AI/Models and adds provider configuration, installation/acquisition, aliases, defaults, route ordering, background routing, fallbacks, privacy, resource and lifecycle controls.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Entries expose stable Dulche model identity plus user-facing name/alias, provider/source, local/cloud/remote state, modalities/capabilities, tool/structured-output support, reasoning controls, context/output limits, loading/availability, privacy/residency, entitlement/cost where known and local RAM/VRAM fit where meaningful. Display names are never used as canonical identity.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The normal picker keeps the primary capability configuration approachable: Chat Model/Route, Image Model/Route and Voice Model/Voice. Advanced exposes Audio Model/Route and Video Model/Route. The user may instead choose one Active Model/Route and allow all compatible capabilities to inherit it, with ordered fallback resolving unsupported capabilities.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Chat is the primary general-purpose route for conversation, reasoning, writing, coding, tool use, agentic work and multimodal chat where supported.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Voice is the first-class conversational/live-voice selection used by Vision & Voice for supported Conversational, Monologue, Live Listener and Live Translate modes. When the selected Voice Model exposes named voices, the user-facing field is labelled Voice and selects VoiceID while showing VoiceModelID as secondary metadata. When there are no named variants the field remains Voice Model.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Advanced Audio covers dedicated transcription, synthesis, audio understanding/transformation or music/audio generation where applicable. Advanced Video covers video generation, editing/transformation or video-native understanding. These category routes may inherit the Active route or use explicit independent ordered routes.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Users may configure a single Active Model/Route for all foreground AI work or assign capability-specific/app/Agent overrides. Separately, a Background Model/Route can be configured for non-interactive work such as background summarisation, indexing/classification, Background Learning processing, permitted Automations AI work, proactive suggestions and other low-priority background tasks.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Foreground and background workloads may use different ordered routes. A user can therefore choose a powerful cloud model first for interactive work while using a small local model first for background work. Users who want simplicity can select a single model and leave fallback entries empty.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: For every routed request Dulche first derives task requirements such as modality/capability, tool use, structured output, context/output requirements, reasoning support and foreground/background role. It then filters candidates against provider/model capability, privacy/locality policy, administrator policy, connection/authentication permission, user fallback policy, entitlement and other hard constraints before considering route priority.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_4
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Conditions that are not model fallback

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Each route and candidate can restrict fallback, including no fallback, local-only fallback, cloud-allowed fallback or provider-specific constraints. A route containing cloud candidates does not itself authorise sensitive context to leave the device. Privacy, administrator and task policies are evaluated before route ordering.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The effective model and routing reason remain inspectable. Home/Dulche records route identity, selected model and skipped/fallback reasons where relevant, for example 'Sol skipped: usage exhausted; Gemma selected' or 'Sol skipped: video-generation unsupported; Fable selected'. This metadata may be surfaced subtly in normal UI and in more detail through diagnostics/Action Graph without cluttering every response.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: LLM Space and Desktop Space overrides MAY exist but remain scoped. Category overrides are independent; for example an LLM Space may override Chat while inheriting global Image/Voice/Audio/Video routes.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Users can assign friendly aliases/nicknames to models. Aliases are presentation conveniences and may be duplicated; all routing objects store stable provider-scoped Dulche ModelID values so duplicate names never create ambiguous execution.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Where supported, the full manager provides discover/install or pull, import, verify, download progress, load, unload, remove, update/replace, rollback, storage-location and compatible CPU/GPU/offload configuration. These operations use Dulche Runtime/Den and provider/package APIs rather than a second model-host implementation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Routes may contain compatible local runtimes, configured commercial/cloud providers, self-hosted/OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Ollama, another Dulche device, enterprise endpoints and authorised provider/Plugin implementations. Provider authentication and credentials remain owned by the appropriate shared credential/provider system.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: For local candidates the picker may show estimated RAM/VRAM requirement, current availability, loading state and reclaimable resources when known. On 9to1-OS this integrates with the AI-aware resource manager; on other Home platforms it uses the available Dulche/runtime resource information without pretending OS-level reclamation exists where it does not.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Managed profiles may limit approved models/providers, acquisition, external cloud use, maximum cost/usage class or fallback destinations. Policy filtering happens before user ordering so reordering a blocked provider cannot bypass a School/organisation restriction.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Home owns the operational permission/trust broker defined by App APIs and automation permissions. It stores and evaluates caller identity, scoped grants, blocks, temporary trust, 30-day Accept and Trust grants, Accept and Always Trust grants, expiry/revocation state and audit history.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Mesh is a Home feature, not a standalone app. It connects authorised user/team devices so selected 9to1 context, projects, Agents and capabilities can operate across devices without requiring every workflow to live entirely in remote cloud infrastructure.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Home owns the shared user-facing Action Graph renderer/source. Dulche owns execution graph/log data and persistence semantics; Home provides the reusable CUI/Markdown presentation component used to display authorised graph data.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Home does not own the primary Voice, Vision or AI Overlay session controls. Those live in Vision & Voice; Home remains responsible only for the shared runtime/model configuration and renderer/platform services they consume.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The Plugins section lists Dulche Plugins enabled/available in the current scope; Skills lists eligible Dulche Skills including the built-in Persistent Skill; Agents lists Agents available through Dulche scope resolution; Files searches authorised files/artifacts without silently granting new access. Availability in the picker never grants permission to execute protected actions or read inaccessible content.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Typed app APIs and shared semantic actions are the normal execution path. Computer Use is not a fallback for missing/failed APIs and remains unavailable unless @Computer Use was explicitly invoked. Permission, review, edit/suggest/view state, conflicts and external-side-effect rules of the target app still apply to cross-app work.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: App-specific document structures remain allowed. Present still owns slides and presentation-level layout; Canvas still owns its infinite spatial surface; Boards owns Board/Page hierarchy and Board-specific layout. The shared engine standardises reusable embedded/shared objects rather than forcing one top-level document model.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Canonical object identity, schemas and style registry

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Windows: Home provides the full native hub/shell, Home Core background services and the Home-hosted Universal Model Picker. Native apps depend on the compatible Home installation/Home Core handshake.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Home owns the shared Node Graph Framework used by Automations and Space graph editors. It is an editing/schema/validation/execution-visualisation framework, not a second automation or AI runtime. Product surfaces register domain-specific events, actions and node types; Dulche and owning apps execute the resulting authorised runtime actions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche is 9-1’s shared llama.cpp-derived local model framework/runtime. One Home-managed Dulche instance serves every 9-1 app through a broker API; apps must never launch their own competing local model servers. It owns model loading, inference lifecycle, resource limits, cancellation and local capability discovery while preserving upstream provenance.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Voice is a Dulche capability. Dulche owns the audio-session runtime, speech/model lifecycle, streaming, interruption and integration with requests, tools, permissions and logs. The user-facing controls live in Vision & Voice rather than Home.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Entry point to the Dulche Voice subsystem for the caller’s current context.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The documented Voice APIs are authoritative but not exhaustive. Additional APIs required for complete voice functionality may be added following Dulche’s existing API conventions and the global API-parity rule.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Translate is a first-class Dulche framework capability for multilingual translation, localisation and cross-language interpretation. It is not owned by a standalone Translate app. The primary user-facing product is the built-in Translate Space, while Write, Mail, Boards, Browse, Vision & Voice, AI Overlay, Sites and other authorised surfaces may invoke Dulche Translate directly for contextual translation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche Translate owns language/locale resolution, translation execution, multi-target Translation Sets, variant identity, glossary/protected-term application, segment alignment, structured-artifact translation contracts, translation job lifecycle, provenance and translation-specific recovery. It MUST use the shared model/provider layer and normal Home/Dulche permission and audit contracts.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A translation request MAY target one or many languages/locales in a single operation. The canonical result is a TranslationSet with stable TranslationSetID, source reference/revision where applicable, source language/locale, request/instruction metadata, glossary references, model policy, created/modified timestamps and one or more TranslationVariants.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Every TranslationVariant MUST have stable TranslationVariantID, TranslationSetID, target language/locale, status, translated content or canonical output reference, revision, provenance, errors/warnings and segment map where available. Retrying, regenerating, manually editing, applying or publishing one language MUST NOT discard successful sibling variants.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Language identity MUST use canonical language/locale identifiers. When a user supplies an ambiguous or unsupported language label, Dulche Translate MUST request/return a structured resolution requirement rather than silently guessing another language.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The built-in Translate Space renders translation work as normal conversation rather than a two-box translator. The selected target-language chips sit immediately above the standard Space chatbar; all source/context selection uses the normal Spaces context architecture.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: When one conversational request returns multiple TranslationVariants, each language variant MUST appear as its own assistant speech bubble. The language/locale name is displayed directly above that bubble. The bubbles are linked as siblings by the same TranslationSetID/request but remain independently addressable for retry, regenerate, edit, apply, export or agentic follow-up.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A prompt may temporarily target a subset/additional language without necessarily changing the Space's persistent language chips. Explicit requests to add/remove/change the default language set update the Translate Space configuration.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Translate MUST support natural follow-up refinement such as 'make the German version less formal', 'keep Action Graph untranslated everywhere', 'add Japanese', 'only redo French', or 'update these because the source changed'. Refinements target the canonical TranslationSet/variant rather than creating unrelated copies unless the user requests a separate result.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Translate Space MAY perform multi-step agentic localisation workflows using normal Space Plugins, Skills, persistent Dulche Agents, Automations and typed app actions. For example, 'translate this page into French, Spanish, German and Italian, then push them to the live site' may resolve the current page semantically, create/update four TranslationVariants, validate each owning artifact/site route and invoke the authorised Sites/WordPress/publishing APIs.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche Translate MUST NOT implement generic hidden publishing or file mutation that bypasses owning apps. Applying translations to Write/Present/Data/Boards/Sites/WordPress/GitHub or other systems uses those systems' canonical typed actions, revision checks, permissions, approvals, audit and idempotency contracts. Partial downstream failure MUST preserve already-successful translations/actions and expose targeted retry.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche Translate MUST translate human-language content while preserving supported non-linguistic structure and identity. For 9to1-native artifacts it should operate through the owning app/shared Productivity Engine using stable object identities rather than flattening the artifact into plain text.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Write translation preserves document structure/styles/tables/images/links/comments and other supported metadata while translating intended text. Present translation preserves slides/layout/theme/text boxes/speaker notes/animations/transitions and detects translated-text overflow instead of silently clipping. Data translation distinguishes human labels/descriptions/comments from formulas, numbers, cell references and identifiers. Boards translation preserves page/block identity and supported embedded artifact references.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Code, commands, URLs, formulas, JSON keys, identifiers, markup/code fences and other structured technical content MUST follow explicit structure-aware rules and MUST NOT be casually translated as prose. The user may explicitly request translation of translatable string literals/comments where the owning format supports safe editing.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Whole-artifact translation SHOULD create a translated derivative/locale variant by default rather than destructively overwrite the source. Explicit in-place commands such as Replace selection with translation use the owning app's normal undo/revision semantics.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Where the source supports stable segmentation, Dulche Translate SHOULD preserve segment identity/alignment between source and each target variant. Segment maps enable side-by-side review, targeted retry, terminology correction and incremental updates.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Translated derivatives MUST retain provenance sufficient to identify source artifact/file/entity, source revision, source/target language, TranslationSetID/VariantID, glossary IDs, model policy and translation time. When the source changes, Translate MUST be able to report that a translation is stale.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Where safe segment identity exists, updating a stale translation SHOULD retranslate only changed/affected source segments while preserving unaffected translated content and user edits. Conflicts between manual target edits and changed source content MUST be surfaced rather than silently overwritten.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche Translate MUST support reusable and request-scoped glossaries. Glossary entries MAY define source term, required/preferred target translation by locale, Do Not Translate, notes/context and applicability scope.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Protected terminology MUST support names, trademarks, product names, case names, technical identifiers, commands and other content that should remain unchanged. Glossary/protected-term application MUST be recorded in translation provenance so unexpected terminology can be diagnosed.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_3
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Text, image, document and media translation

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche Translate MUST support direct text and semantic selection translation. Image/screenshot translation MAY return extracted translated text and, where the selected model/tooling supports it, a translated visual derivative with mapped text regions. Semantic text from a 9to1 surface is preferred over OCR/pixels when available.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: PDF handling MUST distinguish text, scanned and mixed PDFs where detectable. Structured text PDFs should preserve layout/structure as far as supported; scanned/mixed PDFs may require vision/OCR-style extraction. Any layout fidelity loss or uncertain extraction MUST be surfaced before export/apply.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Audio translation may produce translated text and, where supported, translated speech. Video translation MAY produce translated transcript/subtitles and advanced dubbed output where supported. Live realtime interpretation is exposed through Vision & Voice → Live Translate while reusing Dulche Translate language/context/glossary functionality.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche Translate uses the shared Universal Model Picker/model-routing system. Ordinary translation requests SHOULD resolve the highest-quality compatible configured route for the requested languages, modality, context size, latency, privacy/locality, entitlement/cost and tool requirements without forcing the user to manually choose a model.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: An explicit local-only/private policy MUST NOT silently fall back to cloud translation. Unknown language-pair/provider capability is represented as unavailable/unknown rather than fabricated support.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Long or multi-artifact translation MUST use durable TranslationJob state with stable TranslationJobID and statuses such as Preparing, Translating, ReviewAvailable, Applying/Exporting, Completed, Paused, Failed and Cancelled as applicable. Progress MUST derive from real segments/pages/slides/files/variants rather than invented percentages.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Partial failure MUST preserve successful completed segments/variants. A failed page/language/action can be retried independently. Pause/resume/retry MUST not repeat already-completed consequential downstream actions without idempotency/operation identity.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: These are minimum canonical entry points. Applying/publishing translated outputs remains the responsibility of the owning app/Plugin APIs; Dulche Translate returns typed TranslationSet/Variant/artifact references and orchestration metadata rather than bypassing those owners.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche Translate MUST return structured failures including LanguageUnsupported, LanguageAmbiguous, LocaleUnsupported, TranslationModelUnavailable, TranslationCapabilityUnavailable, GlossaryUnavailable, SourceUnavailable, SourceRevisionConflict, SegmentAlignmentUnavailable, VariantNotFound, TranslationSetNotFound, TranslationJobNotFound, TranslationJobNotResumable, StructuredFormatUnsupported, LayoutPreservationUnavailable, PartialTranslationFailure, PrivacyPolicyDenied and ProviderUnavailable in addition to normal Dulche/tool/action failures.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche Translate is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: One request can translate into multiple target languages and returns independently addressable TranslationVariants under one TranslationSetID.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Translate Space places language chips immediately above the normal chatbar and uses normal Space context rather than a separate context row.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Each conversational target-language translation renders in its own assistant speech bubble with the language/locale name above it.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Retry/regenerate/edit of one language does not discard successful sibling language variants.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A conversational request can perform authorised downstream actions such as applying/publishing translated variants only through owning typed APIs.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A partial downstream publish/apply failure preserves successful languages and supports targeted retry.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Write/Present/Data/Boards translations preserve supported structure and do not flatten artifacts into plain text.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Formula/code/identifier content is protected from inappropriate prose translation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Glossaries and Do Not Translate terms apply consistently and remain attributable.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Source revision changes are detected and segment-aware incremental update preserves unaffected/manual target content where safe.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Image/PDF/media translation reports extraction/layout limitations truthfully.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Local-only/privacy policy cannot silently route translation to cloud.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Long/multi-artifact jobs preserve successful progress across pause/failure/retry.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Vision & Voice Live Translate reuses this framework rather than implementing a separate translation engine.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Agents are a first-class Dulche-wide persistent capability layer, not a standalone 9to1 app. Dulche owns the canonical Agent registry, scope/availability resolution, invocation, runs, queues, delegation, capability resolution, lifecycle and recovery. Agent definitions, durable Agent configuration, memory namespaces and relevant persistent run metadata are stored in Den. 9to1 surfaces discover and expose applicable Agents through Dulche.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: AI Studio → Agent Builder is the direct structured authoring/editor surface for this Dulche layer. It creates/edits the canonical Den-backed Agent entity. AI Studio is not the runtime host, and closing AI Studio MUST NOT stop, hide or delete an Agent.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Persistent Dulche Agents are distinct from Dulche Subagents. Agents have stable identity, durable configuration/memory/scope and may exist across many runs. Subagents are transient child-execution units created inside a run for delegation/parallelisation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_3
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Canonical Agent identity and Den persistence

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Every Agent MUST have stable AgentID independent of name plus versioned DefinitionRevision. The Den-backed Agent entity MUST retain at least name, icon/avatar, description, instructions, availability bindings, default model policy, Plugins/Connectors, Skills, Knowledge/Files references, Quick Actions, memory policy, capability/permission policy, delegation policy, graph reference where present, sharing metadata, revision history and lifecycle state.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Renaming, moving scope or changing icon MUST NOT create another Agent. Agent display names MAY collide; AgentID remains canonical. An Agent definition revision used by an active/historical run MUST remain attributable even after later edits.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Den MUST separate Agent definition/configuration from secrets and device-specific executable state. Connector credentials remain secure references; local executable paths/caches do not become portable Agent secrets merely because the Agent syncs through Den.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche MUST support Agent availability scopes including Global, Surface, Space and Project/Entity or equivalent narrower canonical scope bindings. An Agent MAY have multiple compatible bindings when explicitly configured.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Global Agents cascade automatically into every compatible 9to1 surface. Surface-scoped Agents are available only on their declared surfaces. Space-scoped and Project/Entity-scoped Agents appear when the current invocation context matches those scopes. Availability is composed rather than overridden: a narrower scoped Agent supplements applicable broader Agents.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: For a context such as Write inside a Study Space/project, the effective visible set is the compatible union of Global Agents, Write-scoped Agents, current-Space Agents and current Project/Entity Agents, subject to access restrictions. Dulche MUST return origin/scope metadata so CUI can group Agents by Global, current surface and contextual scopes rather than present an unexplained flat list.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Global cascading references the same canonical AgentID everywhere; it MUST NOT create per-app copies. Agent definition updates, memory and run history remain attached to the canonical Agent.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Agent availability and Agent effective permission are separate concepts. A visible Agent may still have actions disabled in the current invocation context.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Effective permissions/capabilities MUST be no broader than the intersection of the Agent definition/instance policy, current surface capabilities, current Space policy, current project/entity scope, caller/user/organisation policy and Home permission/trust state. A surface/Space cannot grant a capability explicitly denied by the Agent/security policy, and a Global Agent does not gain universal data access merely because it is visible everywhere.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_3
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Agent updates — static and reactive animated icons

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Agents MUST support both static image icons and animated avatars. Users MUST be able to choose the presentation for each Agent. The animated-avatar concept is a pet/companion-style icon, using the user's Codex pets/Dots comparison as a design reference, rather than being limited to an unrelated looping image.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Animated avatars MUST react to the Agent's actual activity and relevant conversational events. Required examples include the avatar sitting at a computer and coding while the Agent is coding, and laughing in response to a user joke. Task-state transitions and conversational reactions MUST be configurable and previewable. Reactions are presentation events, not permission grants or claims about hidden reasoning. Animation MUST respect the existing reduced-motion controls and provide a static fallback without losing the Agent's accessible identity or readable activity status.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The canonical Dulche Agent API MUST cover static/animated avatar selection, referenced asset and definition management, animation-state transitions and event/reaction mappings. Use Den-backed stable identities and versioned configuration shared with AI Studio’s visual builder; presentation changes MUST NOT fork the Agent, alter its permissions or leak private content. Verify saved/reopened configuration, static and animated icons, coding activity, joke/laugh reactions, reduced-motion fallback and readable accessible status, including permission-denied and missing-asset recovery. Connect’s Agent-contact contract supplies email, call and text entry points to these same Agents.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Every compatible interactive 9to1 surface SHOULD expose applicable Dulche Agents through the shared AI/Agent picker or a surface-appropriate invocation UI. Apps query Dulche for context-resolved Agents rather than maintaining private Agent registries.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The invocation context MUST be typed and may include SurfaceID, SpaceID, Project/Entity references, ArtifactID, selected ObjectIDs, current semantic context and available typed actions. Dulche filters this context through permissions before supplying it to the Agent.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Surfaces MAY recommend specialist scoped Agents more prominently than generic Global Agents. Recommendation/order MUST NOT change Agent identity or silently select an Agent with broader permissions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: First-party apps MAY ship/register useful surface-scoped Dulche Agent definitions/bindings. Once registered, they are canonical Dulche Agents rather than hidden app-local assistants and can be inspected/edited where policy permits.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Write MAY expose specialist writing Agents such as Editor, Proofreader, Long-form Writer or user-created writing Agents. A Write-scoped Agent can receive authorised semantic document/selection/style/comment/reference context and Write typed actions without becoming available on unrelated surfaces.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Vision & Voice MAY expose a Podcast Agent or similar specialist Voice Agents. A Podcast Agent can accept typed inputs such as Topic, optional Sources, target Duration and Style, then use the Voice Monologue mode to research/plan/generate/play a coherent long-form podcast. It remains a canonical Dulche Agent scoped to Vision & Voice, not a hardcoded private voice feature.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: An Agent definition MAY declare a typed InvocationSchema and optional CUI/Generative UI invocation interface. Surfaces SHOULD render the declared inputs rather than force every Agent through a blank chat box.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Invocation UI definitions MUST bind only to declared Agent inputs and approved typed actions; they MUST NOT grant new permissions. Examples include a Voice Podcast form with Topic/Sources/Duration/Style or a Write rewrite form with Tone, Preserve citations and Scope.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Quick Actions are named manual entry points into a canonical Agent and cascade wherever that Agent is available, subject to each Quick Action's context requirements/visibility rules. They are not separate Agents.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Every QuickAction MUST have stable QuickActionID, AgentID, label, optional icon/description, predefined instruction or named graph entry point, optional typed InputSchema, context requirements, confirmation policy and ordering metadata.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Quick Actions may be context-sensitive. For example, Rewrite selection should appear only where an editable selection exists; a Podcast Agent may expose Make podcast, Continue latest podcast or Create briefing. Invoking one creates a normal canonical AgentRun with standard permissions, Action Graph, side-effect/idempotency controls and run history.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Quick Actions are distinct from Automations. Quick Actions are manually invoked entry points; Automations own recurring, scheduled, event-triggered and condition-triggered execution. An Automation MAY invoke an Agent/Quick Action through the same Dulche APIs.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: An Agent may define Default Model = Inherit or an explicit Universal Model Picker policy. Inherit resolves from the invocation Space/surface/global policy. An explicit Agent default takes precedence over inherited defaults where allowed, while request-specific overrides may take precedence only if Agent/security policy permits.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche MUST capability-check the effective model against the Agent/run requirements such as tools, vision, audio, context or structured output. It MUST not silently cross local/private to cloud boundaries or substitute an explicitly forbidden fallback.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Agent capability bindings reference canonical Dulche Plugins/Connectors/MCP capabilities and Skills by stable identity/version policy. They are not copied into the Agent.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Knowledge/Files references point to Den memory and authorised canonical files/folders/artifacts/providers where possible. The Agent may retrieve current source revisions through owning APIs rather than rely on stale copies. Missing/revoked/incompatible sources or packages MUST be represented explicitly.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Each persistent Agent MUST have an Agent-specific Den memory namespace governed by its memory policy. Durable memory is structured semantic/operational state, not simply an unbounded copy of every conversation/tool result.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Memory writes MUST carry scope/provenance and MUST respect personal/team/shared boundaries. A shared Agent MUST NOT silently copy a participant's private personal Den context, private connected-account data or secrets into shared Agent memory.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Agent memory SHOULD support inspection, conflict handling, deduplication, recency/provenance metadata and removal/disable operations. Secrets encountered in tools/results MUST NOT automatically become durable Agent memory.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A persistent Agent MAY maintain a durable work queue in Dulche. Queue items MUST have stable QueueItemID, AgentID, objective, optional TaskID, priority, creator/trigger provenance, dependencies, status and timestamps. Work may arrive from a user, Space/Task, Automation, another authorised Agent or recovery flow.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A Task is user-level work; an Agent is the persistent worker; AgentRun is a specific execution. The relationship MUST remain explicit: a Task/objective may be assigned to an Agent, which creates one or more AgentRuns. Agents are not themselves a second Task or Automation system.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Each AgentRun MUST have stable AgentRunID, AgentID, DefinitionRevision, objective, trigger/source, optional TaskID/QueueItemID, status, start/end timestamps, effective model/capabilities/permissions, ActionGraphID, outputs, blockers, approvals, usage/budget metadata and recovery/checkpoint state where supported.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Canonical user-facing Agent/run states MUST distinguish at least Idle, Queued, Running, Waiting, Blocked, Paused, Awaiting Approval, Completed, Failed/Error and Disabled as appropriate. Blocked and Awaiting Approval MUST NOT be conflated.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Run controls MUST support Pause/Resume, safe Stop and explicit Cancel where the runtime permits them. Resume continues the same AgentRunID and MUST NOT repeat already-completed consequential actions. Retry of a failed step/run uses idempotency/operation identity to avoid replaying unrelated successful side effects.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Progress UI MUST show truthful objective/current step/known plan progress. It MUST NOT invent a percentage where the Agent cannot estimate completion meaningfully.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche Agent runs MUST create first-class Blocker records for conditions preventing progress, including category, description, time, whether the Agent can self-resolve, required human action and related entities. Agents SHOULD attempt safe recovery of foreseeable recoverable blockers when their contract allows it instead of immediately escalating every failure.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Human-required blockers and pending consequential actions MUST surface through relevant invoking surfaces and Home Events/Notifications/approval UX. Approval remains a Home permission/action decision; Dulche Agents cannot self-authorise through their own instructions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Persistent Agent-to-Agent delegation is a Dulche Agent capability. Delegation MUST retain explicit parent/child AgentRun identities and a typed handoff containing objective, required context references, narrowed capability scope and expected output.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: DelegationPolicy MUST be able to constrain allowed persistent Agents/classes, whether Subagents are allowed, maximum concurrency, maximum depth and applicable token/time/cost/tool budgets. A receiving Agent does not automatically inherit all permissions or memory of its parent.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Persistent Agent delegation remains distinct from Dulche Subagents. Subagents are lighter transient child execution primitives inside the runtime; persistent delegated Agents retain their own canonical AgentID, definition and Den memory policy.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_3
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Action Graph, outputs and operational visibility

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Every AgentRun MUST use the canonical Dulche Action Graph/log/audit pipeline. 9to1 surfaces may render a concise human-readable Activity view and/or the full Action Graph, but they MUST NOT invent a second execution history.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Run outputs MUST be typed references to their canonical owning entities where possible, including Files, documents, Boards, code changes, Planner/Task items, messages, research outputs and other artifacts. Opening an output routes to its owning app/entity rather than copying it into an Agent-only store.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Agent runs, blockers, approvals and outputs may be surfaced contextually in Spaces, Agent Builder Preview, Automations that triggered them, Home Events/Notifications and the invoking app. No standalone Agents app is required or authoritative.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Long-running/background-capable AgentRuns MUST checkpoint enough state to recover or truthfully fail across app closure, Home/Dulche restart, machine restart where supported, provider disconnect or temporary tool failure. Recovery states SHOULD distinguish Reconnecting, Recovering, Recovered and Cannot recover rather than silently restarting from scratch.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Agents MUST support configured runtime/model/tool/delegation budgets such as maximum runtime, spend/tokens, tool calls, concurrent children or delegation depth where the platform can enforce them. Exceeding a budget produces an explicit blocked/failed/approval state rather than uncontrolled continuation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: These are minimum canonical entry points. All Agent Builder and 9to1 surface Agent operations MUST resolve through the same Dulche/Den contracts rather than creating app-private Agent stores or runtimes.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche Agents MUST return structured failures including AgentNotFound, DefinitionRevisionUnavailable, AgentDisabled, AgentUnavailableInScope, AgentBusy, AgentRunNotFound, RunNotResumable, RunRecoveryFailed, QueueItemNotFound, CapabilityUnavailable, PermissionDenied, ApprovalRequired, BlockerUnresolved, DelegationDenied, DelegationDepthExceeded, ConcurrencyLimitExceeded, BudgetExceeded, ModelUnavailable, ToolUnavailable, MemoryScopeDenied, QuickActionUnavailable, InvalidInvocationContext and RevisionConflict in addition to the global Dulche error contract.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche Agents is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: An Agent created in AI Studio Agent Builder is stored as a canonical Den-backed Dulche Agent and remains usable after AI Studio closes.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: There is no authoritative standalone Agents app or duplicate Agent database.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Global Agents appear on every compatible 9to1 surface through Dulche scope resolution without being copied.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Surface-, Space- and Project/Entity-scoped Agents appear only in matching contexts while applicable broader Agents remain available.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Agent availability does not grant permissions; effective capability resolution narrows correctly across Agent, surface, Space, caller and Home policy.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Write can expose/use specialist writing Agents with semantic document context, and Vision & Voice can expose/use a Podcast Agent that drives Monologue mode from typed inputs.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Quick Actions cascade with their Agent, obey context visibility/input schemas and create normal AgentRuns rather than duplicate Agents.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Default Model inheritance/explicit override resolves through the Universal Model Picker without violating privacy/fallback restrictions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Agent memory persists in the correct Den namespace without silently ingesting private/shared-incompatible context or secrets.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
