unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Task → Agent → AgentRun and Automation → AgentRun relationships remain explicit.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Agent queues preserve provenance, priorities/dependencies and durable state.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Blocked and Awaiting Approval states remain distinct and recoverable blockers can be handled autonomously where authorised.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Pause/Stop/Resume/Retry do not replay completed consequential actions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Persistent Agent delegation obeys depth/concurrency/budget limits and does not transfer unrestricted parent permissions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Persistent Agents and Dulche Subagents remain distinct in API, logs and UI.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: AgentRun Action Graph is the canonical execution graph and outputs open canonical owning entities.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Home/Dulche restart can recover supported durable runs or reports Cannot recover truthfully without silently restarting work.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Agent Builder Preview uses the same Dulche semantics while clearly remaining test-scoped.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Agent Builder/other surfaces perform Agent operations through the canonical Dulche Agent API.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Action Graph is a Dulche feature and the user-facing structured view of an AI/agent execution log. It turns the underlying request history into an inspectable graph rather than requiring users to read a raw continuous log.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The graph can show prompts, model calls, thinking/response phases where available, tool calls, AI actions, approvals, dependencies, retries, generated artifacts, failures, hard errors, blockers and timestamps. It is derived from Dulche’s audit/tool/full-log data so the graph and logs describe the same execution rather than separate histories.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Returns the structured Action Graph for a request, including the data needed for CUI/Markdown rendering.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: RestartFrom forks/restarts the prompt or agent run from the selected point while preserving the original history. Earlier completed actions remain auditable; actions after the restart point are re-executed as a new branch and remain subject to current permissions/approval requirements.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche produces the Action Graph data and the CUI/Markdown representation needed to render it. The shared renderer source lives in Home and is reusable across the ecosystem, so apps do not need separate implementations.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Any app may surface the renderer where useful. For example, Spaces may expose a Show Action Graph button for a response, while Home can expose the same graph from logs or activity history.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche Runtime provides a simple, consistent API for starting, configuring and controlling model endpoints without requiring each app or harness to manually manage model-server lifecycle.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Starts a local Dulche endpoint on the specified port. Local Start requires an explicit port; Start(Remote(...)) instead requires an explicit remote target.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Checks whether Dulche is reachable on the specified port.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Sends a prompt/instruction to the specified endpoint.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Sets the model used by the specified endpoint.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Sets the temperature used by the specified endpoint.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Suspends model activity while keeping the model and its context loaded.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Stops the model and clears the endpoint/port.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Sets the endpoint's reasoning level. level may be a named effort such as low or medium, or a percentage. Percentages are mapped across the reasoning levels exposed by that model. For example, if a model exposes five reasoning levels, the 0-100 range is divided across those five levels and the matching level is selected.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: For endpoint-wide commands other than Start, an omitted/null port targets the active endpoints authorised in the caller's scope. RequestID-based controls are never broadcasts. Return per-endpoint outcomes, retaining partial failures and isolated sessions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Returns the list of ports currently used by Dulche.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Sends the prompt/instruction to all active endpoints.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Endpoints can be created and configured as one unit. Example:

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: // Other supported model/endpoint properties may also be configured here.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Timeout is disabled by default. When set, an endpoint that remains inactive for the specified number of seconds is automatically paused rather than stopped, preserving the loaded model and context.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche natively provides the persistent Agent layer, Subagents/parallelisation, command usage, code execution, local and cloud models, tool calling, MCPs, Plugins, Skills and Generative UI. MCPs, Plugins and Skills are first-class extension types with stable identity, lifecycle, permissions, validation and dedicated APIs; they MUST NOT exist only as ad-hoc wrappers around generic tool calls. Persistent Agents are Den-backed durable Dulche entities, while Subagents are Runtime child-execution primitives. Capabilities can be disabled within scope when they are not permitted or required.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_3
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche MUST expose a canonical request-aware Tool Registry describing the tools, executable capabilities and usable resources that a model can employ to satisfy a request. The registry is broader than a literal list of function names: it includes first-party 9to1 app actions/APIs, Automations actions, Plugins, MCP tools, callable Agents, Skills that contribute executable workflows through authorised dependencies, Files/resource retrieval, image/audio/video generation capabilities, code/shell tools, web/network tools where permitted and other registered Dulche capabilities. Computer Use is represented only when it has been explicitly invoked under the Computer Use contract.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Every registry entry MUST use stable identity and structured metadata. At minimum it exposes ToolID/CapabilityID, source type and owner, version/revision, human-readable name, action IDs, semantic capability/intent tags, supported input/output types, parameter schemas, prerequisites, permission scopes, side-effect/risk classification, platform/scope constraints, availability/health and whether user approval or additional configuration is currently required. Display name and wording of an action MUST NOT be the sole mechanism used to decide what a tool can do.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche MUST derive an EffectiveCapabilitySet for each request from the canonical registry. The effective set is filtered by the active user/profile, current app/Space/project, installed/enabled package state, app/API availability, explicit @ invocations, platform capability, privacy policy, administrator policy, current permissions/trust and any request-specific restrictions. Installed-but-unavailable, available-but-unapproved and immediately executable capabilities MUST remain distinguishable.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The active model/orchestrator MUST be given an inspectable, context-budget-aware representation of the EffectiveCapabilitySet. Dulche MAY provide a compact high-level catalogue initially and expose query/search APIs for deeper inspection so very large tool inventories do not consume the model's entire context. Capability discovery MUST nevertheless remain available throughout the request and MUST refresh when packages, permissions, target apps or connection state materially change.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Tool selection MUST be intent-based rather than exact-name-based. Dulche MUST translate the user's requested outcome into one or more semantic intents and compare those intents against tool capability metadata, schemas and declared examples/aliases. A tool does not need an action whose literal name matches the user's wording when its underlying capability can satisfy the requested effect.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: For example, a request such as 'remind me tomorrow at 4 PM' MUST be resolvable to a time-triggered Automations operation even if no action is literally named CreateReminder. The semantic requirement is a durable time-based trigger that produces the requested notification/action. Likewise, 'create an image of ...' MUST resolve to an eligible image-generation capability such as the first-party image app/tool or an installed authorised image-generation Plugin, even if the tool's action is named Generate, Render, Imagine or another equivalent verb.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Capability resolution MUST support composition. If no single tool can fulfil the complete request but a sequence of authorised capabilities can, Dulche MUST be able to construct a typed ResolutionPlan whose steps pass structured outputs/references between tools. For example, a request to 'create an image and put it on the title slide' may resolve to image generation followed by Present insertion; a request to 'find the file and email it' may resolve to Files search followed by a Mail/Plugin send action, subject to normal permissions and approvals.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: ResolutionPlan steps MUST identify the selected ToolID/CapabilityID, action, required arguments, expected outputs, dependencies, permission/approval state and why the step satisfies part of the user's intent. Capability resolution is planning, not execution: selecting a feasible tool MUST NOT bypass its normal permission, approval, confirmation, privacy, cost or side-effect rules.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Before a model states or implies that 9to1 cannot perform a requested digital action, it MUST first perform capability feasibility resolution against the current EffectiveCapabilitySet unless the impossibility is already established by a current authoritative hard constraint. The model MUST NOT answer 'I cannot directly create images', 'I cannot create reminders', 'I cannot access files' or equivalent merely because the base model itself lacks that native capability when Dulche exposes an authorised tool path that can perform it.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A capability that exists but is missing a prerequisite MUST be described as blocked/configuration-required rather than impossible. Examples include ApprovalRequired, PermissionDenied, AccountConnectionRequired, MissingRequiredInput, AppUnavailable, ProviderUnavailable, CapabilityDisabledByPolicy and UnsupportedOnCurrentPlatform. When the missing prerequisite can be resolved within the current request and permission bounds, Dulche SHOULD resolve it or ask only for the specific user decision/input required and then continue.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: If several feasible tools can perform the same intent, Dulche MUST select according to explicit user invocation/instruction first, then applicable app ownership/canonical-data rules, privacy/locality policy, capability fitness, permissions, reliability and configured user preferences. Cost/latency MAY participate where policy allows. Dulche MUST NOT choose an unrelated or lower-fidelity tool merely because its action name more closely resembles the user's wording.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Explicit @ invocation remains authoritative. An @Plugin, @App, @Agent, @Skill or other invocation narrows or prioritises the capability source according to that invocation's contract. However, ordinary natural-language requests do NOT require the user to know or name the underlying tool. 'Create a presentation', 'set a reminder', 'generate an image' and similar outcome requests MUST be sufficient for Dulche to discover and use the appropriate capability when one is available.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Skills, Agents and Files participate according to their real semantics rather than being falsely treated as identical callable functions. A Skill may contribute instructions/workflow/tool dependencies; an Agent may be invoked as a delegated execution capability; a File/resource may provide required input/context; an App/Plugin/MCP/native action may perform the mutation. The resolver MUST be able to combine these heterogeneous entries into one plan while preserving their distinct identities, permissions and audit records.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche MUST expose canonical discovery operations equivalent to Dulche.Tool.List(context?), Dulche.Tool.Search(intent, context?), Dulche.Tool.Get(toolID), Dulche.Tool.Resolve(intent, context?) and Dulche.Tool.ExplainResolution(resolutionID). Resolve MUST return either one or more ranked feasible ResolutionPlans or a structured no-feasible-path result containing the evaluated hard constraints and missing prerequisites. Search/Resolve MUST use semantic capability metadata in addition to lexical names.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The Runtime MUST cache capability metadata efficiently but MUST version/invalidate the cache when relevant package versions, app capabilities, connection state, permissions, policy or provider health change. A model MUST NOT continue relying on a stale 'tool unavailable' conclusion after the capability registry has materially changed during the request.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A tool-result or retrieved document MUST NOT be able to self-register new authority merely by claiming that another tool exists or should be allowed. Registry membership and permissions come from trusted Dulche/Home registration, package manifests, app capability contracts and current policy. Semantic discovery MUST therefore improve capability use without creating a prompt-injection route to invented tools or escalated permissions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Failure to resolve a tool path MUST be truthful and inspectable. Dulche MUST distinguish NoMatchingCapability from MatchingCapabilityUnavailable, MissingPrerequisite, PermissionBlocked and PolicyBlocked. When no feasible path exists, the model MAY explain the limitation, but it MUST NOT fabricate a tool or claim to have performed the action. The Resolution attempt and selected/no-selected candidates MUST be visible in FullLog/Action Graph at an appropriate level of detail.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_3
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Acceptance coverage MUST verify at minimum that: a reminder request resolves to an Automations time-based workflow without requiring the phrase 'automation'; an image-generation request invokes an eligible image capability rather than returning a false inability statement; a presentation request can resolve to Present from another app; a multi-tool request produces a dependency-ordered ResolutionPlan; explicit @ invocation overrides automatic source choice; permission/configuration blockers are distinguished from true impossibility; Computer Use does not appear unless explicitly invoked; and removal/disablement of the only matching capability causes a structured no-feasible-path result rather than a fabricated success.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Subagent is the Dulche Runtime term for a child execution unit created by a request or another Subagent to delegate work and/or execute independent work in parallel. Subagents are execution primitives, not persistent Dulche Agents and not Den-backed Agent definitions. The public API MUST use the names Subagent and Dulche.Subagent for this capability so callers cannot confuse subagent parallelisation with persistent Agents.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A Subagent MAY execute one or more model/tool steps and MAY create nested Subagents within inherited limits. Every Subagent belongs to exactly one RootRequestID and, except for root execution, exactly one parent request or parent Subagent. Detached/orphan Subagents are outside the current contract; child work MUST remain causally attached to its parent tree.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Constructing a Subagent object MUST NOT execute work. Construction only defines an inspectable configuration object. Execution begins only when submitted through Dulche.Subagent, preventing object construction from causing hidden model/tool/external side effects.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Start creates one child and returns its handle after identity/state allocation. StartParallel submits the supplied definitions as sibling children under the same parent and returns one handle per child in input order. StartParallel grants permission for concurrent scheduling; it does not guarantee simultaneous execution when endpoint, provider or resource limits require queueing.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Wait returns that child’s terminal Result. WaitAll returns one terminal outcome per requested child and MUST preserve child identity even when one or more children fail. WaitAny returns when the first requested child reaches a terminal state and identifies that child. Join operations MUST NOT flatten or discard per-child errors, blockers, logs, token usage, model provenance or tool records.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Every Subagent MUST expose SubagentID, ParentSubagentID?, ParentRequestID, RootRequestID, SessionID, EndpointID, Depth, State, CreatedAt, StartedAt?, FinishedAt?, Model and its effective tool/permission/budget configuration. IDs MUST be stable for the lifetime/history of that execution and MUST NOT be derived from display names, array position or queue position.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Subagent State MUST distinguish at least Created, Queued, Running, Waiting, Pausing, Paused, Completed, Failed, Blocked, Cancelled and TimedOut. Waiting means the Subagent is suspended awaiting dependencies/children and MUST NOT retain an execution slot that prevents those dependencies from running.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Ordinary requests on one endpoint remain serial by default as defined by the Runtime queue contract. Subagents do not silently change that rule. A parent waiting on a child that requires the same endpoint MUST yield its execution slot so the child can run; this is mandatory anti-deadlock behaviour.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Sibling Subagents assigned to different eligible endpoints MAY execute concurrently subject to resource, provider and configured concurrency limits. Siblings assigned to the same endpoint execute serially unless that endpoint explicitly advertises concurrent execution and the request enables the supported parallel mode.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Model = Auto and Endpoint = Auto permit the Runtime scheduler to select an eligible model/endpoint using declared capabilities, permission/privacy constraints and resource policy. An explicitly selected Model or Endpoint MUST NOT be silently replaced merely to increase parallelism; inability to satisfy the explicit selection returns a structured scheduling/capability failure.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: MaxParallelChildren is a hard upper bound on concurrently Running children beneath the configured parent scope. Children above that limit remain Queued. Runtime-wide endpoint/resource limits MAY further reduce actual concurrency but MUST NOT increase it above the declared limit.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Context inheritance is explicit. Supported policies are None, Inherit and Selected(...). Inherit snapshots the authorised parent context at spawn time; it does not create unsynchronised mutable shared conversation state. Selected(...) copies only the declared messages/context objects/references. None starts without parent conversational context except identity/control metadata required by Runtime.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A child Result becomes visible to the parent through an explicit join/result path or another explicitly authorised shared data object. Child completion MUST NOT silently rewrite earlier parent messages or a sibling’s context. Multiple children MUST NOT concurrently mutate the same session history without an explicit revision/conflict mechanism.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A Subagent MUST NOT acquire more authority than its parent/caller. Effective child authority is the intersection of the caller’s current authority, the parent’s effective authority and the scopes requested for the child. The same narrowing rule applies to tools, filesystem/data scopes, external integrations, network access, credentials and action approvals.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Permissions = Inherit and Tools = Inherit copy only currently effective parent scopes. Expired/revoked grants are not inherited and no new approval is created by spawning a child. An action that requires approval in the parent context still requires approval when attempted by a child. Subagent creation MUST NOT provide privilege escalation or approval bypass.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Subagent budgets are hierarchical. Descendant consumption contributes to the ancestor/root aggregate for tokens, time, steps, tool calls and cost. A child MAY request stricter limits than its parent; it MUST NOT enlarge any hard parent/root limit. Parent and root budget exhaustion prevents further descendant work from starting and stops or blocks active descendants at safe boundaries according to the relevant resource type.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: SubagentBudget MUST support MaxTokens, MaxTime, MaxSteps, MaxToolCalls and MaxCost where those quantities are enforceable. Runtime resource policy MAY additionally constrain CPU, GPU, RAM, VRAM and endpoint occupancy. Provider-unavailable cost/token telemetry MUST use the Runtime’s existing null/Na rules and MUST NOT be treated as zero consumption.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Actual descendant consumption MUST be attributed to both the child and its ancestor aggregates without double-counting the same invocation. If the system reserves budget before dispatch, reservation and settlement MUST be visible separately from actual settled usage.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: SubagentLimits MUST support MaxChildren, MaxParallelChildren and MaxDepth. MaxChildren counts direct children created by the configured execution scope. MaxDepth is measured from the root request, whose depth is 0; its direct Subagents are depth 1. Creating a child that would exceed a hard limit MUST fail before child execution begins.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The Runtime MUST also enforce implementation-wide safety ceilings even when the caller requests larger values. The effective limit is the minimum of caller/request limits, inherited parent limits and Runtime/provider limits. Limit failures return stable structured codes including MaxChildrenExceeded, MaxDepthExceeded and ConcurrencyLimitExceeded.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Parallel sibling execution MUST retain independent terminal outcomes. One child failure MUST NOT erase successful sibling results. The parent/join operation receives a structured collection containing, for every child, SubagentID, terminal State, Result?, Errors?, Blockers?, FinishReason and relevant usage/telemetry.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: SubagentFailurePolicy MUST support at least Collect, FailFast, RequireAll and BestEffort. Collect waits for requested children and returns every outcome. FailFast requests cancellation of still-unfinished siblings after the first terminal failure/blocker while retaining already completed results. RequireAll treats any non-successful required child as a failed join. BestEffort permits the parent to continue with successful children while preserving explicit failed/blocked/cancelled outcomes.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Failure policy changes orchestration/join behaviour only; it MUST NOT suppress logs, errors, blockers or completed side effects. External actions already completed by a failed/cancelled child are not automatically rolled back unless the action itself defines rollback semantics.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Stopping a root request MUST stop all unfinished dependent descendants. Stopping a Subagent MUST stop its unfinished descendants but MUST NOT automatically stop its parent or independent siblings; the parent receives the child’s Cancelled outcome and applies its configured failure policy.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Pausing a parent MUST prevent it from dispatching new child work. Running dependent children follow the parent’s explicit pause policy: PauseChildren requests safe-boundary pause, LetChildrenFinish permits already-running children to complete, and StopChildren cancels them. If no policy is supplied, PauseChildren is the default.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Restart creates a new attempt for the targeted Subagent using the specified/current authorised context and preserves the prior attempt in history. Restart MUST NOT replay already completed consequential tool/external actions automatically. Replacement/cancellation of an ancestor MUST invalidate stale descendant approvals and provisional output.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Persistence and recovery of subagent trees

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche Den MUST persist the execution-tree metadata required to inspect and recover Subagent work: stable identities, parent/child relationships, request/attempt revisions, effective configuration, states, checkpoints, results, blockers/errors, tool/action records and durable side-effect evidence. Runtime remains the execution authority; Den is the durable record.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Checkpoint(rootRequestID) creates a durable tree checkpoint for all checkpointable active descendants. Restore(checkpointID) reconstructs the tree from the latest compatible durable state. Exact continuation is allowed only when the underlying model/backend/tool supports it; otherwise Restore MUST expose that it is a continuation/restart from checkpoint rather than claiming byte-for-byte execution resumption.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: On crash/restart, completed external/tool side effects MUST be reconciled from durable records before any step is retried. A restored tree MUST NOT repeat a non-idempotent completed action merely because the parent process lost volatile state. Uncertain side-effect state becomes a Blocker requiring reconciliation or approval.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Action Graph MUST render Subagent execution as an explicit causal tree/graph. Each Subagent is a distinct node/branch linked to its parent and MAY contain model calls, tool calls, approvals, outputs, child Subagents, blockers and errors. Parallel siblings MUST be visually distinguishable as concurrent branches rather than flattened into a fabricated sequential order.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Subagent graph nodes MUST expose at least SubagentID, state, parent/root identity, model/endpoint, start/end/duration, token/usage data, tools/actions, errors/blockers and child count subject to permissions/redaction. Restart-from-here on a Subagent node creates a new attempt/branch under the existing historical tree and MUST NOT rewrite the original branch.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Runtime FullLog MUST retain causal parent IDs and per-execution sequence numbers. Parallel/nested timing MAY overlap; aggregate timing MUST NOT sum overlapping spans as if they were serial. Token/model/tool aggregation MUST use the existing no-double-counting rules for parent and child invocations.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Subagent operations add stable structured failures including SubagentNotFound, MaxChildrenExceeded, MaxDepthExceeded, ConcurrencyLimitExceeded, BudgetExceeded, DependencyFailed, CheckpointUnavailable and RestoreConflict. These follow the Runtime error contract and MUST NOT rely on free-form string parsing.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Subagent support is implementation-complete only when automated/representative acceptance coverage verifies all of the following:

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: One parent spawning and joining one child with preserved parent/child identity.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: StartParallel with multiple siblings on different endpoints demonstrating actual concurrent execution where resources permit.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Same-endpoint child dependency without deadlock and without silently enabling unsupported backend parallelism.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Context None/Inherit/Selected isolation, including no sibling context leakage.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Permission/tool inheritance cannot exceed parent/caller authority and still triggers required approval.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Nested descendants obey MaxDepth, MaxChildren and MaxParallelChildren exactly.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Hierarchical token/time/step/tool/cost budgets stop or block descendants at the correct boundary without double-counting usage.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Collect, FailFast, RequireAll and BestEffort preserve the documented per-child outcomes.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Root/child stop and parent pause propagation follow the documented dependency semantics.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Checkpoint + process restart + Restore reconstructs the tree without replaying a completed non-idempotent side effect.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Action Graph renders parent/child/nested/parallel branches with stable IDs and correct causal relationships.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Telemetry preserves overlapping parallel spans and model/token/tool attribution without parent/child double counting.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Subagent API failures return the documented structured error codes.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The user's Den may store models using both a stable ID and a user-facing name. Either can be used for lookup. User-facing names are not required to be unique.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Returns the model matching the supplied ID.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Returns all Den models matching the supplied user-facing name, including their IDs.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Models.toml contains the models available to the current Dulche configuration and the capabilities/properties associated with them.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Returns the configured model matching the supplied ID.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Returns all configured models matching the supplied property. A property may describe a capability, such as reasoning support, or an identifying property such as an ID.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche can resolve a model directly from a local directory, with support for as many compatible model file types as practical.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Where an operation fails because the requested model cannot be resolved, Dulche returns "model not found" rather than throwing an exception.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche can discover and obtain models from supported sources including llama.cpp, Ollama and Hugging Face.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Checks whether the requested model exists at the specified source.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Lists models from the specified source that match the supplied property.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Pulls a model temporarily. A pulled model survives endpoint suspension, but is discarded when the endpoint is stopped.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Replaces one model with another. When no replacement policy is specified, Dulche applies the safe replacement policy: preserve only metadata explicitly classified as model-independent (for example a user-facing alias), recalculate model-derived capabilities/limits from the replacement artifact, and reset configuration values that are invalid or unsupported by the replacement. Immutable artifact/model identity MUST NOT be copied from the old model.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Preserves compatible properties from the old model where possible.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Replaces the model without preserving its previous configuration.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: safe MAY be specified explicitly as the preservation policy. Under safe, only fields classified by the replacement schema as model-independent/safe-to-carry MAY be preserved; all model-derived or compatibility-sensitive fields MUST be recalculated or reset.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Documented API names, argument order, Result field names and explicit behaviours are binding and must be implemented verbatim. This is not an exhaustive API list: compatible overloads and missing APIs may be added. Resolve unspecified edge cases using the same simple, predictable, inspectable and permission-aware philosophy; do not silently rename or reverse an existing operation. The requirements below extend and clarify the earlier examples.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Retain port-based calls and add Dulche.Prompt(prompt, port) and Dulche.Prompt(request, endpoint). Request contains input/messages, SessionID, model selection, generation settings, permitted tools, output schema, streaming preference and limits. Input supports text, images, audio and authorised file/document references through capable adapters; other modalities are capability-gated. No private context/file is sent remotely without the required permission.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche.Prompt(port) and Dulche.Prompt() remain shorthand for an explicitly prepared request in the caller's scope. Add Dulche.PreparePrompt(prompt) to prepare caller-local input for those shorthand calls; consume a snapshot at submission and never reuse another caller's input. Without prepared input, return MissingPrompt. Explicit prompt/request overloads avoid hidden state and are preferred in concurrent code.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Assign RequestID immediately, before queueing. SessionID owns conversation/context; EndpointID identifies the logical execution target; port/URL identifies transport. Shared endpoints do not imply shared sessions. Add Dulche.CreateSession(endpoint) and session lookup/reset/close plus scoped context export/restore. Context is the token-window budget, not conversation identity. Overflow returns ContextExceeded unless the caller explicitly permits documented truncation/summarisation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The remote overload connects to an authorised remote target. It does not assume permission to manage the host's entire service. Targets declare provider, base URL, model identity, credential reference, transport/security settings and capabilities. Local Start requires a port; remote Start requires an explicit remote target. Return an endpoint handle with identity, state and structured failure information, never a false Ready state. Cloud targets do not require invented local ports.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Return Result using the exact field names below. The question mark denotes optional content, not part of the field name. Empty metrics return null. Provider-unavailable metrics return Na, serialised as the exact JSON string "Na" and exposed by typed bindings as an unavailable sentinel. A measured zero remains 0. This applies to all metrics, including those not originally marked optional and nested model metrics.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Use value/null/Na-capable types and separate availability/provenance metadata for pending, disabled/redacted, measured, estimated and provider-unavailable values. Never substitute zero or an invented value for unavailable data. Required identity/status and the Runtime event-log container remain present. Collections with no applicable entries may be null; numeric counts may be a measured zero. A complete aggregate cannot silently ignore unavailable contributions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Text: the actual user-facing response, separate from tool arguments and undisclosed provider internals. No text may have been produced for a blocked, cancelled or non-text-only response.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Thinking: the thinking log actually exposed and permitted by the model/provider. Label traces and summaries distinctly; never present a summary as the complete internal thinking or reconstruct undisclosed reasoning. Empty content is null; provider-unavailable thinking is Na.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Tools?: identities of the distinct tools actually used, with links to invocations. Tools offered but not called are not counted as used.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Sources?: sources retrieved, supplied or cited, with provenance and relevant response-span references. Distinguish retrieved evidence from unverified model-generated citations.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: GeneratedUI?: structured, versioned UI data, separate from Text and rendered only through an explicit CUI integration.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Models: models actually used, including agent/subtask models, in first-use order and deduplicated by artifact/provider revision. Preserve roles, call counts, endpoints and invocation records. Models[i].Parameters exposes the individual parameter metric.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Also return RequestID, SessionID, Endpoint, Status, FinishReason, request revision and attempt identity. FinishReason distinguishes Completed, Cancelled, Replaced, Blocked, Error, OutputLimit and Refused. Paused is a non-terminal state, not successful completion. Preserve the original provider finish reason separately.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Earlier shorthand fields are compatibility views: Reasoning maps to Thinking; Model identifies the primary responding model; TokenUsage groups the token metrics; Error is the primary error from Errors. ToolCalls contains individual invocations, while Tools is their tool-identity summary. Endpoint identifies the primary request endpoint; additional endpoints remain in Models and logs.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: TimeElapsed: wall-clock seconds from acceptance to terminal result, including queueing/pauses; live snapshots measure through the snapshot time. Expose queue, pause and execution duration separately.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: TimeThinking?: attributable thinking duration. TimeAgentic?: duration of agent/tool work. TimeResponding: duration of generating the actual response. Use backend events or observed spans, not an assumption that all pre-first-token delay is thinking. Parallel and nested spans may overlap, so phase totals need not sum to TimeElapsed; report timing basis and estimate status.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: InputTokens: input processed by all included model invocations. OutputTokens: output generated by those invocations, including reported non-visible reasoning/tool output where applicable. TotalTokens equals InputTokens plus OutputTokens when both are known. Preserve provider tokenisation, cached-token details, modality usage and billing data per invocation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: ResponseTokens: output tokens attributable to the user-facing response. AgenticTokens?: output tokens attributed to agent orchestration/tool-call work. ThinkingTokens?: backend/provider-reported thinking tokens. These are labelled subsets of OutputTokens, not extra quantities to add to it. Subsets can overlap, such as thinking within an agent step; retain attribution rather than inventing a mutually exclusive split.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Aggregate actual invocations, including retries, within an explicit request/attempt/task scope. Do not double-count a child invocation through both parent and child totals. If a contributing provider withholds a required metric, the complete aggregate is Na; return a separate known subtotal and coverage when useful. Supported metrics with no value yet are null.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Parameters: architectural parameter totals across distinct model revisions actually used, counted once per model rather than once per prompt/instance. This is not a claim that several models behave like one larger model. Report per-model total and active MoE parameter counts separately when known, and label declared architectural active counts versus observed routing.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Location: structured model-weight placement with a readable form such as "9.3% GPU | 90.7% RAM". This is residency, not utilisation. Include device IDs, measurement time/window, quantity basis, sampling method and any other/unknown location. Do not confuse parameter share with byte share, or include KV cache/activations as model weights. Shared/unified memory must not be double-counted.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: MoEs expose separate Active and Total placement views. State the denominator: an active-set distribution normalises to the active set; active weights expressed as a share of all parameters must be labelled accordingly. Keep underlying quantities. A display such as "Active: 19.9% GPU | 20.1% RAM; Total: 6% GPU | 94% RAM" needs an explicit basis and remaining share; do not silently normalise or fabricate missing placement. Hidden provider placement is Na.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Storage: disk bytes occupied by response-associated model artifacts, not VRAM/RAM, token usage or cumulative download traffic. Deduplicate shared artifacts within each physical storage location and show local/device/remote breakdowns. Unknown remote storage makes the complete total Na, while a known local subtotal may be shown. Distinguish persistent versus temporary artifacts.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: AuditLog?: timestamped reads, writes and other actions, with actor, request/attempt, target, permission/approval, start/end, outcome and side effects. ToolLog?: every tool invocation with ID, tool/version, timestamps, safe arguments/results, outcome and correlation IDs. Tools is the summary; ToolLog is the invocation history.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: FullLog: the continuous ordered collection of Runtime-observed actions, model calls, available thinking/summary events, tools, queue events, pauses, replacements, retries, approvals, results, blockers and errors. Include UTC timestamps, per-request sequence numbers and causal parent IDs. Do not fabricate exact global ordering for concurrent work. Stream/paginate large logs without losing continuity. Undisclosed provider internals are not promised; sensitive payloads are redacted/permission-filtered with omissions recorded.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Blockers?: structured reasons work cannot complete, with affected scope, evidence, attempted recovery, whether human input is needed, next action and retryability. Errors?: hard model/provider/Runtime/tool failures with stable code, message, component, timestamp, request identity and safe details. A blocker need not be a crash; cancellation need not be a hard error. Keep recoverable retries/warnings in logs.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Use structured results for ModelNotFound, MissingPrompt, EndpointNotFound, PortInUse, InvalidArgument, OutOfMemory, ContextExceeded, ProviderUnavailable, AuthenticationFailed, PermissionDenied, UnsupportedCapability, ToolFailed, RequestNotFound, InvalidState, QueueFull, Conflict and ModelLoadFailed. Preserve "model not found" as the friendly message for resolution failure. Expected operational failures must not depend on string parsing or unhandled exceptions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Streaming means delivering text pieces and events as they become available rather than waiting for the whole response. It changes delivery, not the intended answer. Add Dulche.PromptStream(prompt, endpoint) and Request.Stream while retaining a path that awaits one completed Result.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The submission handle exposes RequestID, Status, a final-result awaitable and optional event stream. Events include text deltas, permitted thinking/summary deltas, tool/approval events, validated UI changes, metrics and states. Include request/revision/attempt, sequence and timestamp. The final event contains the same Result contract as non-streaming, including final metrics or null/Na.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Never execute partial tool arguments or arbitrary partial markup. Mark provisional output and discard stale deltas after replacement. Reconnect using a cursor or current snapshot without starting another generation or replaying an external action. Use bounded buffering/backpressure with explicit gap/snapshot recovery; no silent audit-event loss. Closing a display stream does not automatically cancel its task.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Stop that response, not the endpoint. Cancel queued work or halt running generation/future tool dispatch at a safe boundary; retain partial output/logs and return Cancelled. Repeated stops are idempotent. Dependent unfinished child work is cancelled, not unrelated requests. A completed external action is not automatically undone.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Pause the response, retain its output/context and prevent dispatch of its next steps. Report Pausing until a safe boundary is reached, then Paused. Paused work stays paused until resumed/stopped, not silently completed.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Resume paused work. Use exact continuation only when the backend supports it; otherwise return UnsupportedCapability or an explicitly disclosed, authorised continuation/restart mode. Buffering output while the provider keeps generating is not an exact pause. Never repeat completed tool side effects automatically.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Interrupt the current response with the new prompt at a safe boundary, ahead of ordinary queued work. Preserve interrupted state and return a linked RequestID for the priority prompt. The default stacked interruption resumes the interrupted request afterwards where supported and still applicable; superseded/cancelled work must not be revived. Multiple stacked interruptions use last-in-first-out order and a bounded nesting limit.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Queue a new prompt after the referenced request in its session without interrupting it; return a new RequestID. Commit session context in order. Failure/cancellation must not silently discard queued input: expose its dependency/state and revalidate its context before starting.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Replace the targeted prompt, such as after a message edit. Retain logical RequestID, increment revision and create a new attempt. A queued replacement retains its position; a running replacement supersedes/cancels the old attempt at a safe boundary; a paused replacement stays paused; replacing a completed prompt creates a fresh response attempt from the relevant prior session state. Preserve earlier actions/output in history, invalidate stale deltas/approvals and never automatically undo external actions or replay subsequent turns.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: If response A is running on an endpoint, ordinary response B is queued by default, even if its backend permits parallel generation. Other endpoints may work independently within resource limits. Queue order, position, capacity and timeout are observable. Optional parallel mode cannot silently change this serial default. A task waiting for a child on the same endpoint yields its execution slot to the dependency rather than deadlocking its own queue.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Paused work may yield to independent sessions, but dependent work in the same session cannot overtake it. Recheck permissions/context before dispatch. Controls cannot target another user's work without authority. Remote tool cancellation is best-effort when a tool cannot stop; record actual completion/side effects rather than falsely claiming cancellation succeeded.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Add endpoint state inspection, explicit Resume, capability discovery and health events. Distinguish Starting, Loading, Ready, Busy, Pausing, Paused, Stopping, Stopped and Failed, plus model Downloading, Installed and verification states. Reachability is not model readiness.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Endpoint Pause retains local weights/context and suspends its work. Stop cancels its queued/running work, unloads owned resources and releases the port without deleting installed artifacts or Den history. Remote operations affect Dulche's own requests/sessions unless remote lifecycle control is supported and authorised. Manual pause requires resume; inactivity pause may auto-resume on new work with an event. Inactivity Timeout is distinct from request, queue, tool and network timeouts.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Snapshot model identity and effective settings per attempt. SetModel, SetTemperature and SetReasoningLevel apply to future work unless safe mid-run reconfiguration is explicitly requested. Validate temperature, output limits, top-p/top-k, seed, stops, penalties and structured schemas against capabilities; silently ignoring an unsupported requested setting is not success.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Reasoning percentages map to ordered supported levels: for n levels use min(n-1, floor(p*n/100)) for p in 0..100; reject out-of-range percentages. With five levels, 0-<20 selects the first, 20-<40 the second, and 80-100 the fifth. Named levels must resolve to advertised support; do not invent a mode.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Home owns the shared 9to1 Dulche broker/service. Multiple managed endpoints do not justify each app spawning competing unmanaged servers. Resource policy covers CPU/GPU selection, offload, RAM/VRAM budgets, active models, scheduling and explicit eviction. Pause does not promise memory release while weights remain loaded; pressure must not silently switch models or discard private context.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Provider adapters declare credentials by reference, capabilities, privacy/residency information, rate limits and bounded backoff/retry. Model/provider fallback must be configured and permission-compatible, never silently send local/private context to a cloud. Record actual fallback models and usage. Recover with Den checkpoints; reconcile uncertain non-idempotent actions before retry.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Add Dulche.GetCapabilities(model) and endpoint capability inspection. Separate model ability, adapter/backend support, host integration and granted permissions. A supported modality grants no automatic access to microphone, camera, files, shell or network. ToolCallsAllowed = All means all tools already permitted for that caller/request. Support None, ReadOnly, selected-tool policies, scope overrides, consequential-action approval, sandboxed code and revocation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: GeneratedUI is returned as data. A CUI developer explicitly implements <GenerativeContainer> and advertises supported schemas/components/actions. Without it, retain a usable text/data fallback rather than assume rendering support. Validate components, properties, limits, references and action bindings; model output never becomes trusted executable application code. UI actions use authorised typed tools tied to the request/revision. Invalid generated UI is isolated/logged without crashing the app or losing Text.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Agents/tool loops require bounded step/time/token/cost budgets, visible progress, loop detection, approvals and cancellation. A proposed tool call is not proof of execution. Retrieved content and tool results cannot grant permissions or override the caller's restrictions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Preserve Den, Models.toml, local-directory, FindModel, ListModels, Pull, Install and Replace APIs. Adapters resolve supported artifacts/catalogues; a runtime backend is not assumed to be a universal registry. Pin/verify source revisions and expose download progress, cancellation, resumption and required storage. Unsupported formats return errors instead of false compatibility claims.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Temporary Pull ownership is tied to a consuming endpoint/request scope. Stopping releases that ownership; delete bytes only when no other live or persistent owner needs them. Install makes ownership persistent. Replacement stages/verifies the new model, applies preserveConfig/wipe/safe compatibility, records identities and supports rollback without deleting an in-use model. Logical IDs/aliases may survive; immutable artifact identity must reflect the replacement.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Expose runtime/API/schema versions, states, queues, tokens/context, memory/storage, rate-limit status, time to first output, generation throughput and trace IDs through permission-filtered diagnostics. Use Na for unavailable telemetry, null for empty telemetry and labels for estimates. Publish SDK/adapter conformance tests and compatibility negotiation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Acceptance covers serial A/B queueing, streaming/non-streaming parity, every response control, queued/running/paused/completed replacement, null/Na/zero, withheld provider metrics/thinking, token aggregation, MoE denominators, scoped broadcasts, context isolation, unsupported exact resume, tool retry/cancellation, generated-UI fallback, provider failure, memory pressure and recovery.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: PersistencePolicy MUST support at least Standard and Persistent. Standard retains the ordinary Runtime finish/timeout/checkpoint behaviour defined elsewhere. Persistent is a durable root-request policy intended for work that should continue until its user-visible completion predicate has been satisfied.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A Persistent request MUST define or derive an inspectable CompletionContract from the user's request, active Skill requirements and target-app acceptance criteria. Completed is valid only when required outputs exist, required validation/verification has run where applicable, required target mutations are confirmed and no required work item remains Pending, Running, Retryable or Blocked. A checkpoint, partial deliverable, progress report or model statement such as 'done' is not itself completion evidence.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Soft request duration limits, provider execution leases and internal scheduling slices MUST NOT terminate a Persistent request merely because a continuation boundary was reached. When continued execution requires a new model invocation, endpoint lease or recovered process, Dulche MUST create a linked attempt under the same RootRequestID, restore the latest safe state/checkpoint and continue. Completed consequential actions MUST be reconciled before retry so persistence does not duplicate side effects.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Persistent requests MUST remain cancellable. Pressing the user-visible Stop control targets the root persistent request, requests safe-boundary cancellation of unfinished dependent work and produces the normal Cancelled result with retained partial output/logs. Persistence MUST NOT reinterpret an explicit user Stop as a transient interruption to auto-resume.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: While a Persistent root request is active, ordinary user messages sent through the same compose surface are SteeringMessages belonging to that root request. They are appended durably, ordered by receipt sequence and presented to the orchestrator at the next safe planning boundary without terminating the current turn. They MUST NOT be implemented as ReplacePrompt or StopResponse, and MUST NOT cause already completed actions to replay.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Persistent orchestration MUST maintain a dependency-aware work graph. A structured Blocker marks only the work nodes that depend on it. When a blocker needs user action or permission that the agent cannot obtain itself, Dulche surfaces the blocker and continues every runnable node that does not depend on it. If all remaining nodes are blocked, the root state becomes AwaitingUser; AwaitingUser is non-terminal and keeps recovery/checkpoint state until the user resolves, changes or explicitly stops the task.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Budgets, administrator policy, permission boundaries and hard safety restrictions still apply. Persistence MUST NOT convert a denied action into an allowed action or silently purchase/consume resources beyond configured policy. A limit that can be changed by the user becomes a structured blocker; a hard non-overridable policy restriction remains recorded truthfully and the request continues any unaffected work.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Persistent state MUST survive supported Home/Dulche restarts. Den MUST retain RootRequestID, request revision, CompletionContract, task/dependency state, SteeringMessages, blockers, checkpoints, completed side-effect evidence, active Skill versions and attempt lineage required to resume without fabricating progress or repeating consequential work.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Context compaction is a first-class Dulche Runtime capability, not an app-specific prompt trick. Dulche MUST track the effective context budget for every model invocation and MAY initiate automatic compaction before hard exhaustion using model/provider-specific safety margins. Apps and Agents consume the same canonical compacted session state rather than implementing incompatible private compaction.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Compaction MUST preserve semantic obligations required to continue the task: current user instructions and constraints, active permissions/trust decisions, CompletionContract, outstanding tasks and blockers, accepted decisions, stable object/file/artifact IDs, current revisions, completed consequential actions, verification evidence, relevant source provenance and any exact values whose precision is required. Redundant conversational phrasing, duplicated status chatter and obsolete intermediate reasoning MAY be reduced.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Compaction MUST be non-destructive to durable history. The original authorised conversation, tool records and artifacts remain in Den according to retention policy; the compacted context is a derived execution view with provenance back to source message/event ranges. A model MUST NOT be told that omitted content never existed merely because it is outside the active compacted view.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: If ordinary compaction cannot create enough safe context without materially losing required information or required media fidelity, Dulche MUST transition to Context Summarisation rather than silently dropping required content or returning ContextExceeded immediately. Typical triggers include a conversation dominated by images/media that cannot be reduced further without unacceptable information loss, unusually dense tool history, or a model whose effective context limit is smaller than the preserved minimum working set.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Context Summarisation is a distinct Dulche job. A summariser model reads the retained conversation/history section by section using bounded windows so the summariser's own context cannot overflow. Each section produces a structured intermediate summary containing obligations, facts, decisions, identifiers, artifacts/references, completed actions, unresolved work/blockers, provenance and continuity notes. Dulche then performs one or more bounded merge passes until a final execution summary fits the target context budget.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Section boundaries MUST be deterministic and provenance-preserving. A merge MUST NOT discard a requirement merely because it appears only once. Conflicting instructions or facts MUST remain represented as a conflict with source references instead of being flattened into an invented resolution. Exact code, identifiers, numeric values, legal/technical constraints or other precision-sensitive content that cannot be safely paraphrased MUST remain as pinned excerpts or stable references rather than approximate prose.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Images, audio, video and other large artifacts SHOULD remain out-of-band as stable artifact references wherever the target model can retrieve them on demand. Context Summarisation MAY summarise authorised derived observations/metadata, but MUST NOT claim that visual or media detail was preserved if the summariser could not inspect it. Required uninspectable media remains a blocker or retained reference, not fabricated text.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A local summariser model MAY be used automatically when an eligible local model is available under the configured routing/policy. Sending conversation content to a cloud summariser requires explicit user permission for cloud Context Summarisation or an existing user setting that clearly grants that permission for the relevant scope. A cloud-capable model in an ordinary fallback route does not by itself grant permission to upload context for summarisation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: If cloud summarisation is required to continue, permission is absent and no eligible local summariser can satisfy the job, Dulche MUST surface ContextSummarisationPermissionRequired/ContextCapacityBlocked as a non-destructive blocker. Persistent requests enter or remain AwaitingUser as necessary rather than losing history or pretending the task completed.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche MUST expose canonical operations equivalent to Dulche.Context.Compact(sessionID, options?), Dulche.Context.Summarise(sessionID, options?) and Dulche.Context.GetState(sessionID). Results MUST report source ranges/revisions, target model/context limit, method, summariser ModelID when used, retained pinned items, omitted/referenced artifacts, token estimates where available and whether the resulting context is sufficient for the next invocation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Computer Use is a first-class Dulche capability but MUST be opt-in per request. It is enabled only by an explicit @Computer Use invocation token or an equivalent explicit user control that resolves to the same ComputerUseInvocationID. An ordinary natural-language request, an @App mention or failure of a typed app API MUST NOT silently activate Computer Use.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The Computer Use capability may control eligible graphical applications through supported pointer, keyboard, accessibility/automation and visual-interaction primitives. It SHOULD use the fastest reliable state channel available, including accessibility/automation metadata where appropriate, avoid unnecessary human-speed delays, batch safe independent interactions where supported and verify state transitions instead of relying on fixed sleeps. Speed MUST NOT weaken verification or permission gates.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: By default, the first attempted interaction with each target application in a Computer Use run requires user approval for that AppID/process identity, and changes to application or operating-system settings require approval before mutation. Home settings MUST allow the user to change this policy to automatic approval for eligible apps and to an Approve All eligible-apps policy. Persisted approval policy remains scoped by user/profile, app identity and the normal Home trust/permission model.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Auto-approve and Approve All MUST NOT bypass hard exclusions, administrator policy, OS security boundaries or other non-overridable safeguards. Computer Use receives no more filesystem, network, credential, settings or app authority than the invoking user/request already possesses.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Generic Computer Use MUST NOT attach to, send input to, automate or manipulate game executables or anti-cheat-protected game surfaces, including games launched or managed through platforms such as Steam or Epic Games Launcher. When classification is uncertain and anti-cheat/game automation risk is plausible, the target is ineligible by default. This exclusion exists independently of user trust level because generic automation can create account/anti-cheat risk.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The game exclusion does not prohibit Dulche Agents from participating in games deliberately configured through the 9to1 Play framework. Play interaction MUST occur through Play's typed GameDefinition/Match/contestant actions and capability isolation, not by using generic Computer Use to drive an external game client.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Every Computer Use run MUST produce an inspectable action stream with target app/window identity, action type, timestamps, relevant pre/post state evidence, approvals, failures and side effects. Sensitive screen regions, credentials and typed secrets MUST follow the normal redaction and permission rules; logs MUST NOT become a second plaintext credential store.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche Autoreview MUST inspect proposed and recent Computer Use actions continuously. It MUST flag patterns including repeated identical or near-identical actions without progress, repeated failing commands, oscillation between states, privilege escalation, bulk/destructive deletion, destructive shell commands such as rm -rf or platform equivalents, security-setting changes, suspicious executable/download flows and other high-risk sequences. High-confidence imminent destructive risk MUST be able to pause the next action for review rather than merely add a passive warning.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Autoreview findings are structured ProblemEvents and MUST feed the shared Problem handling contract. A Computer Use recovery intervention MUST preserve the current request, state and logs and SHOULD redirect to a safer or more direct interaction strategy. It MUST NOT hide that a risky action was proposed or attempted.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_3
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Thinking logs, work state and ETA

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Thinking-log presentation is a first-class Dulche feature backed by Runtime events. Home MUST expose one global user preference with the modes Precise, Concise, Detailed and Ramble; compatible apps inherit it unless an explicitly supported per-surface override exists. If no preference has been set, Precise is the default.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Precise shows only thinking/work events that materially advance the task, such as a resolved decision, discovered blocker, completed verification step or changed plan. It MUST suppress repetitive self-talk and events that do not change task state.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Concise renders short activity summaries suitable for rapid scanning, for example 'Moving a square', 'Opening Browse', 'Checking the build' or 'Waiting for approval'. These summaries MAY be generated from richer telemetry but MUST remain faithful to the underlying action/state.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Detailed exposes substantially more model/provider-permitted reasoning trace and task rationale, including intermediate decisions and why a strategy changed when that information is actually available and permitted. It MUST still distinguish observed facts, tool results, summaries and model reasoning.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Ramble exposes the maximum provider/model-permitted thinking/work trace available to Dulche, including abandoned approaches, self-corrections and changes of mind when the provider actually supplies those events. Ramble MUST NOT reconstruct, infer or falsely label undisclosed private chain-of-thought as if it had been exposed by the model/provider.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Thinking mode changes presentation only. It MUST NOT change the model's configured reasoning effort, tool permissions, stored audit truth, Action Graph or provider privacy rules.
