Provider-unavailable thinking remains Na/Unavailable under the existing Result contract.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: While active, permitted thinking/work events render inline in chronological position with the conversation rather than in a separate hidden console. The visual treatment MUST be lower-emphasis/ghost-like relative to user/model message text while still meeting accessibility contrast requirements and MUST use non-colour cues so users can distinguish message content from thinking/work content.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: When the active thinking/work phase ends, the inline region collapses under a disclosure labelled 'Thought for <duration>' when no tool/action execution occurred, or 'Worked for <duration>' when one or more tools/actions were executed. Duration uses the Runtime's active execution span for that phase rather than queue time. Expanding the disclosure restores the permitted events according to the selected display mode.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: After 60 seconds of continuous active execution in one foreground 9to1 turn, Dulche MUST request an ETA from the active orchestrating model through a canonical ETA request. The model returns an estimated completion timestamp plus optional confidence/reason. The UI displays the timestamp in the user's locale/time zone and clearly marks it as an estimate, not a guarantee. Paused/AwaitingUser time does not count as continuous active execution.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche MUST expose an operation equivalent to Dulche.RequestETA(requestID). An ETA response includes RequestID, AttemptID, EstimatedCompletionAt, GeneratedAt and optional Confidence/Reason. If the active model cannot provide a meaningful estimate, the result is explicitly unavailable; Dulche MUST NOT invent a timestamp. Material replanning MAY request an updated ETA and MUST replace rather than stack stale estimates in the primary UI.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Problem handling is a first-class Dulche Runtime capability for detecting, surfacing and recovering from common model/agent failure modes without forcing every app to implement its own ad-hoc watchdog.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The canonical ProblemType set MUST support at least Looping, NoProgress/Stuck, Repetition, HallucinationOrFabrication, OverAgreement/Sycophancy, InstructionDrift, ContradictionWithGroundedState, RepeatedToolFailure, UnsafeActionPattern and Other/UserReported. Additional typed categories MAY be added versionably without collapsing distinct existing meanings.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Loop detection MUST consider semantic and action-level repetition, not only identical text. Examples include repeatedly issuing the same failing command, alternately undoing/reapplying the same mutation, reopening the same surface without new evidence, recreating completed work or repeatedly restating the same answer while the task remains unfinished.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Hallucination/fabrication detection SHOULD use available grounded evidence such as tool results, canonical app state, source provenance, stable object IDs and completion evidence. Dulche MUST flag fabricated claims of completed actions, nonexistent files/entities/tool results or unsupported factual assertions when confidence is sufficient; it MUST NOT treat disagreement with an unverified model statement as proof that the user is wrong.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: OverAgreement/Sycophancy detection SHOULD flag responses that materially adopt or endorse a user's factual premise, conclusion or requested assessment without adequate evidence when the task calls for grounded evaluation. Recovery prompts the model to re-evaluate the evidence and user request; it MUST NOT mechanically disagree with the user merely to appear independent.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: When automatic detection reaches its configured intervention threshold, Dulche creates a ProblemEvent and injects a clearly identified Runtime recovery directive at the next safe boundary. The directive tells the model what failure pattern was detected, relevant evidence and the required correction, such as stop repeating the command, reassess grounded state, use a different strategy or verify the claimed result. Runtime recovery directives MUST NOT be forged as user-authored messages.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: If the detected problem is associated with a proposed consequential or dangerous tool/Computer Use action, Dulche MAY pause dispatch before the action and require re-planning or applicable approval. Lower-risk reasoning-quality problems SHOULD normally correct the active request without cancelling the turn or discarding valid completed work.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Every conversational 9to1 AI surface MUST expose a small Problem pill above/adjacent to the compose bar. The user can invoke it even when automatic detection did not fire, select a ProblemType and optionally add a note. Manual reports enter the same ProblemEvent/recovery pipeline and are delivered to the active request at a safe boundary without implicitly stopping the request.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: ProblemEvents MUST record stable ProblemEventID, RequestID/AttemptID, category, detector source (automatic, autoreview or user), timestamp, safe evidence references, confidence when machine-detected, intervention taken, affected action/node and resolution outcome. They MUST appear in FullLog/Action Graph with sensitive content redacted as required.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Problem detection MUST itself be bounded and loop-safe. A false-positive recovery that does not improve state MUST NOT trigger an endless reviewer/model ping-pong. Repeated unresolved problems should escalate to a visible blocker, alternate model/strategy where permitted, or user decision while preserving completed work.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche Den is Dulche's persistent, cross-harness storage standard. It allows Dulche state to remain available across compatible apps and harnesses rather than being tied to one running endpoint or one application session.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A user's Den can maintain their model catalogue using stable model IDs alongside user-facing names. IDs provide unambiguous model references; names are intended for human-facing use and may be duplicated, which is why name lookup returns a list rather than assuming a single match.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Den is also intended to provide persistent storage for cross-app context, agents and related Dulche state so compatible 9to1 surfaces can share the same underlying information instead of maintaining isolated copies.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Den is a directory-based persistent store with a versioned den.json manifest, structured records, a transaction journal and separately stored or referenced large objects. Portable records use UTF-8 JSON; local databases and indexes may accelerate access but must not be the only readable copy or create an incompatible private format. Exports contain authorised records and explicitly selected attachments. Reference model weights and external Files documents by identity/content hash rather than copying them by default. No special bundle extension is mandated.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The manifest identifies DenID, FormatVersion, SchemaVersion, minimum reader/writer versions, namespaces, storage locations and required capabilities. Validate manifests, paths, sizes and hashes before import. Importing never executes code or automatically enables agents, tools, connections or permissions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Every model, agent, conversation, context object, workflow and request has a stable ID independent of name/path. Separate personal, team, organisation and app namespaces; device paths and hardware settings stay device-local. Shared namespaces are opt-in.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Model records contain logical ID, display name, aliases, provider/source, immutable revision/artifact hash, family, format, quantisation, modalities/capabilities, context/output limits, ordered reasoning levels, configuration overrides, installation references, timestamps, provenance and replacement history. Parameters, active MoE parameters, storage and hardware metrics use Runtime's availability rules. Local paths are not portable identities.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: ID lookup is unambiguous in its namespace. Name/property lookup returns all matches, never silently chooses a duplicate. Aliases are explicit namespace-scoped references. Model replacement may retain logical ID/name but records changed artifact/provider identity, retained/reset settings and rollback history.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Den persists messages/revisions, authorised context, agent definitions, requests/results, tool records, approvals and checkpoints as distinct record types. Runtime executes work; Den stores information needed to inspect or resume it.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Portability covers supported messages, context, configuration, definitions and history, not arbitrary backend caches, GPU state or undisclosed internal model state. Checkpoints declare backend/model compatibility. Distinguish a continuation attempt from exact resumption and never automatically repeat completed external actions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Context records identify source, owning app, timestamps, author/inference provenance, access scope and retention. Distinguish user-authored, imported and inferred context. Sharing a conversation does not automatically share its referenced sources, secrets, attachments or private inferences.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Persistent Memory is a core Dulche Den subsystem for durable cross-session information about the user, recurring entities, preferences, decisions, projects and other scoped context that Dulche should be able to retrieve in future conversations or authorised surfaces. It is separate from Background Learning.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Memory is not one opaque prompt file. A persistent MemoryEntry should carry stable identity, content or structured value, subject/entity, memory type/category, scope, source/provenance, confidence where applicable, created/updated state, supersession/correction relationships, retention state and user-edited/locked state where supported.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Memory can be scoped so unrelated Agents/apps do not receive unnecessary context. Supported scopes should include global/user memory plus narrower project, Agent, app/surface or other explicit contexts where appropriate. Retrieval MUST respect both scope and permission.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche may create or update memories from eligible conversations/context according to the user's Memory Frequency and memory policy. Retrieval is relevance-based: only memories useful to the active request/context should be injected, rather than the complete memory store.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Explicit user corrections supersede contradictory earlier memories. Den MUST retain enough provenance/revision information to distinguish an explicit user statement from an inference and to avoid repeatedly resurfacing a memory that has been corrected, superseded or deleted.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Settings MUST expose a Memory Frequency preference with exactly four user-facing levels: Never, Sometimes, Often and Always. The selected level controls how readily Dulche autonomously creates, reinforces or updates Persistent Memory from eligible non-temporary interactions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Never: Dulche MUST NOT autonomously create, reinforce or update Persistent Memory from ordinary interactions. Direct user-invoked memory-management actions are separate explicit operations.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Sometimes: use a conservative threshold and retain only clearly durable, repeatedly useful or high-value information.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Often: use a lower threshold and remember useful preferences, decisions, entities and ongoing context more readily when they are likely to help future responses.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Always: evaluate every eligible interaction for durable memory and normally retain information that satisfies the memory policy, while still deduplicating noise, respecting scope/retention rules and avoiding ineligible information.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Changing Memory Frequency affects future autonomous memory behaviour; it MUST NOT silently delete existing memories. The setting is independent of Background Learning.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Spaces can provide Temporary Chats. Persistent Memory creation is disabled inside a Temporary Chat regardless of the user's Memory Frequency. While a chat is temporary, Dulche MUST NOT autonomously create, update, reinforce, merge or promote Persistent Memory from that conversation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Any explicit action that would save new Persistent Memory from a Temporary Chat must be unavailable or clearly report that memory creation is disabled for temporary chats. Temporary-chat memory-write suppression MUST NOT be bypassed by an Agent, plugin, Skill, tool or Background Learning pipeline.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: This rule governs memory creation/writes. Whether existing authorised memories are retrieved into a temporary chat is a separate context/privacy policy and MUST NOT be inferred from the memory-write prohibition.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Users must be able to inspect, search, edit/correct, supersede and delete persistent memories through the appropriate settings/Den surfaces. Deletion and retention use Den's normal lifecycle, sync and purge contracts. Memory export/import must preserve scopes, provenance and deletion/supersession semantics rather than flattening entries into plain prose.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Persistent Memory exists as a distinct Den record system and is not substituted by Background Learning, session context or Agent-only memory.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Memory retrieval is relevance-, scope- and permission-aware.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Never/Sometimes/Often/Always control autonomous memory creation/reinforcement with the semantics above.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Temporary Chats in Spaces cannot create, update or reinforce Persistent Memory regardless of frequency or calling surface.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Corrections/supersession are durable and user-manageable, and explicit user statements remain distinguishable from inference.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Authorise access per principal, namespace and object/action. Reading context, modifying an agent, executing tools and administering Den are separate permissions enforced below the UI. Revocation applies to future reads/searches/executions; it does not erase copies already disclosed.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Store credential references, not plaintext API keys, passwords, private keys or tokens in records, exports or logs. Resolve references through secure credential storage on the relevant device/service. Protect sensitive storage and transport, document key ownership/recovery and redact sensitive log payloads without falsifying whether an action occurred.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Use atomic transactions or crash-safe journalled updates. Mutable objects have revisions; updates supply expected revisions and return Conflict instead of overwriting newer data. Support concurrent readers and coordinated writes with bounded locking. Operation IDs make safely retryable writes idempotent.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Validate before commit, preserve the previous valid record until commit and recover/quarantine incomplete writes after crashes. Export consistent snapshots. Caches and indexes are rebuildable, not the sole authority.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Cross-device/team sync is optional and namespace-scoped. Track IDs, revisions, origin device and deletion tombstones. Offline changes wait for an authorised sync target. Merge compatible disjoint edits; preserve conflicting versions for review. Wall-clock timestamps alone never choose the winner.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Concurrent conversation edits create explicit revisions or alternate continuations. Sync does not execute stored requests or replay tools. Device-local paths, secrets and hardware settings are not portable values. Recheck permissions on reconnection and record deletion/restoration/revocation explicitly.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Support create/open, inspect/search/update, export/import, backup/restore, soft-delete and explicit permanent purge. Retention is configurable and visible by namespace/category; do not assume indefinite retention or silently discard work under storage pressure. Soft-delete preserves recoverable revisions until expiry. Purge covers managed replicas/indexes/derived records under policy, with explicit limits for offline copies and external backups.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Large files use content-addressed blobs or authorised external references. Reference counting prevents deletion while another owner needs an artifact. Distinguish quotas for metadata, logs, caches, attachments and model weights. Den metadata does not make a temporary Pull permanent: Install or an explicit pin creates persistent ownership.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Publish versioned schemas, examples and conformance tests. Compatible writers preserve unknown optional fields; unknown security-critical fields or required capabilities block unsafe writes. Validate, back up and transactionally migrate schemas. Unsupported newer versions may open read-only when safe, never discard fields to force a downgrade.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Round-trip null for empty metrics and Na for provider-unavailable metrics, serialised as "Na"; measured zero stays 0. Permission-filter search/index results and include revision/provenance.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Preserve Dulche.Den.GetModelByID(id) and Dulche.Den.ListModelsByName(name). Add compatible create/open, scoped search, revision-checked update, export/import, sync, restore and purge APIs with documented signatures and failures.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Acceptance covers cross-harness round-tripping, duplicate names, concurrent edits, offline conflicts, crash recovery, revocation, safe import, secret-free export, model replacement/rollback, retention/restore and migrations without data loss.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Generative UI is a Dulche capability that allows a model or Agent to return arbitrary structured user interfaces when an interface is more useful than prose. Generated interfaces may be visual, interactive and stateful, but MUST be expressed through a validated declarative Generative UI schema and MUST NOT execute arbitrary model-generated application code.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: CUI is the rendering layer for Generative UI. Generated surfaces render inside a CUI <GenerativeContainer> or equivalent trusted host component using approved CUI primitives, design tokens, theming, layout, accessibility and interaction behaviour. Any authorised 9to1 app may host a GenerativeContainer without implementing its own incompatible renderer.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche may choose the structure and composition of the interface, including novel layouts, but the model output is data/schema rather than executable JavaScript, Python, shell commands, native binaries or arbitrary application code. The Generative UI runtime validates schema version, component types, properties, state bindings, declared actions and capability references before rendering.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Generative UI provides reusable high-level templates for common interaction patterns. Templates are starting structures, not hard limits; Dulche can instantiate, extend, combine or restyle them through supported schema properties.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Table, sortable/filterable data table and comparison grid.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Quiz, practice exercise and answer/reveal workflow.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Diagram, relationship map and structured visual explainer.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Other shared templates added by the Generative UI framework or authorised extensions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: When no template fully fits the task, Dulche can compose a custom surface from approved lower-level primitives. The supported primitive set should include, where appropriate, text/heading blocks, icons or generated illustrations, cards, badges/tags, buttons, inputs, dropdowns, toggles, sliders, chips, lists, tables, grids, tabs, accordions, progress indicators, layout containers, drag containers, drop zones, connectors/relationships, semantic-object views and other safe CUI primitives.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The primitive library is extensible through versioned framework/extension contracts. Unsupported component types MUST be rejected or downgraded safely; a model cannot create a new privileged executable component merely by naming it in the schema.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Generated surfaces may maintain bounded typed state. Supported interactions can include selecting options, sorting/filtering, expanding/collapsing content, progressing through steps, editing fields, revealing hints/answers, checking responses, reordering items, dragging supported objects between declared drop zones, switching views and updating selected data.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: State mutations are handled by the Generative UI runtime or by declared typed actions. Interaction support does not grant the model arbitrary code execution or unrestricted access to the host application's process.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A generated surface is a first-class conversation artifact and may evolve across turns. Dulche should be able to patch or transform an existing surface instead of rebuilding unrelated output from scratch. Examples include turning a static explanation into an interactive exercise, adding another column to a table, converting notes into flashcards, adding filters, changing a card grid into a comparison view or preserving quiz progress while adding new questions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Updates must address stable SurfaceID/component/state identities or equivalent schema identities so user interaction state is retained wherever the requested transformation allows it. Partial regeneration is preferred when only part of a surface changes.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Generated controls bind to declared typed actions rather than arbitrary executable handlers. An action definition includes stable identity, expected input schema, allowed state mutation or API binding, required capability/permission and result/error contract.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Pure presentation and local interaction may execute inside the Generative UI runtime without external side effects. Actions that invoke 9to1 APIs, tools or external services remain subject to the same permission, confirmation, auditing and consequence rules as the underlying capability. Generative UI MUST NOT be a path around security prompts or tool permissions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Generative UI can bind to authorised structured data and canonical 9to1 entities instead of flattening everything into prompt text. Examples include Data ranges, Planner tasks, Maps Places/Routes, Board items, Write selections/documents, search results, translation sets, code diffs or Dulche Action Graph state.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Bindings retain source identity and permissions. A rendered card or table row that represents a canonical object should reference that object rather than silently creating a disconnected copy unless the user explicitly asks for a snapshot.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A generated surface may remain ephemeral to the current response/session or be promoted through an explicit supported conversion/save path. Examples include saving generated flashcards as a study resource, converting a generated task board into a Board, inserting a generated table into Write/Data or saving a generated route through Maps. Promotion uses the destination app's canonical API and permissions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Generative UI may reproduce the functional idea or spatial structure needed to explain a third-party product/game without copying proprietary artwork merely to imitate the source. Where licensed/authorised assets are not available, it should use generic, stylised, text-labelled or newly generated representations sufficient to communicate the concept.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Example: if the user asks how an item is crafted in Minecraft, Dulche may create a visual 3x3 crafting-grid representation using generic/stylised ingredient tokens and an output slot rather than copied official item textures or proprietary interface artwork. In later turns the same surface may be made interactive using approved drag/drop primitives so the user can move ingredient tokens, receive validation, request hints or turn the recipe into a quiz.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Generated UI MUST inherit the host CUI theme/design system and remain accessible. The runtime should enforce semantic roles, labels, focusability/order, keyboard operation, screen-reader information, non-colour-only meaning and accessible alternatives for interactions such as drag/drop wherever the component library supports them.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Invalid, unsupported or unsafe generated schemas MUST fail closed without executing arbitrary content. Dulche may repair/regenerate the affected surface or fall back to a non-interactive/native representation while preserving the user-visible answer where possible.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Result.GeneratedUI contains the generated UI payload when present and returns null when no generated interface is produced. The payload must identify schema version, surface identity, component tree, declared state/bindings and declared actions/capabilities required to reproduce the surface safely.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche can create arbitrary useful UI structures without arbitrary code execution.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Built-in templates and lower-level CUI primitives can be combined and extended within the declarative schema.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Generated surfaces support safe stateful interaction and can evolve across conversation turns without unnecessarily discarding user state.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: All external side effects route through typed permission-aware actions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Structured 9to1 data can be bound by canonical identity, and generated artifacts can be promoted through destination-app APIs.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Generated UI follows CUI theming/accessibility and safely handles invalid schemas or unavailable components.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Background Learning is an explicitly opt-in Dulche personalisation subsystem. It is separate from Persistent Memory. Enabling Background Learning allows Dulche to learn useful patterns, interests and reusable knowledge from eligible 9to1 activity over time; it does not itself enable or disable Persistent Memory and it does not imply continuous fine-tuning of the underlying base model.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Background Learning can maintain three broad classes of learned information:

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: 9to1 usage and project context: which authorised surfaces the user uses most, recurring workflows, recently or frequently active projects, apps commonly used together, important project terminology/entities and other usage patterns that improve contextual relevance.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Interests and topic Knowledge Banks: recurring subjects the user appears to care about, together with reusable factual/reference material that can improve later answers and remain available offline. For example, repeated questions about cars may lead to an Interest record for cars and a local Cars Knowledge Bank containing useful terminology, concepts and sourced reference material.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Other relevant personalisation information: additional permitted information that materially improves responses, such as preferred terminology, recurring goals, explanation preferences, established project conventions, frequently used tools, entity relationships and corrections that should influence future response behaviour.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The usage-learning layer SHOULD retain useful semantic state rather than an indiscriminate permanent clickstream. For example, it may learn that Dev and Stack are frequently used for a particular project or that a project is currently active. Raw activity used to derive these signals should be retained only to the extent required by the configured retention/privacy model.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Learned project context can help Dulche resolve ambiguous references, rank context candidates, suggest likely relevant surfaces and prepare authorised Agents with useful project context. It MUST remain scope-aware: project-specific learning does not automatically become unrelated global context.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Background Learning can create and maintain topic-specific KnowledgeBank entities. A KnowledgeBank can contain a stable ID, topic/title, entries, source/provenance metadata, confidence, freshness, creation/update state, storage/sync policy and enabled/disabled state. Knowledge Banks may be created automatically from recurring interests or explicitly managed by the user.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Knowledge Bank entries may include reusable summaries, terminology, relationships, reference facts and other material previously obtained from authorised local sources, user interactions or trusted retrieval. Factual entries MUST retain enough provenance/freshness information for Dulche to distinguish durable knowledge from information that may need refreshing.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Knowledge Banks are not the same as Persistent Memory. For example, 'the user is interested in cars' is personalisation/user context; a structured offline bank explaining engines, EV charging and vehicle terminology is subject knowledge. Dulche may use both when relevant, but they remain separately inspectable and manageable.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Background Learning MUST store structured learned records rather than relying on one opaque free-form profile. Records should carry stable identity, category/type, subject/entity, learned value, provenance, confidence, creation/update state, last reinforcement/use where useful, freshness/expiry semantics and user-edited/locked state where applicable.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Explicit user corrections outrank contradictory inferred learning. If a user corrects an inferred preference, project status or interest, the system MUST revise/supersede the stale inference instead of allowing both to compete indefinitely as equally valid facts.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The complete learning store MUST NOT be injected into every request. Dulche must retrieve only learning context relevant to the active request, Agent, app and permission scope. Retrieval should use current entities/topics/project context to select the smallest useful set of records and Knowledge Bank material.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Background Learning data is private by default and exists to personalise the user's 9to1 AI experience. It MUST NOT be sold, used to build advertising profiles or indiscriminately uploaded to third parties. Enabling Background Learning does not itself grant permission to transmit learned information to a cloud model/provider.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: If a Dulche request uses a remote/cloud provider, disclosure of any learned context remains subject to the normal provider, privacy, permission and data-minimisation rules for that request. The implementation MUST distinguish permission to learn/store information from permission to disclose that information externally.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Any optional cross-device synchronisation of Background Learning state must be user-controlled and protected by the applicable authenticated/encrypted 9to1 sync/storage architecture. The feature MUST remain useful locally and must not require insecure cloud upload merely to personalise responses.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Users must be able to enable/disable Background Learning, pause new learning, inspect learned information, inspect and manage topic Knowledge Banks, correct inaccurate learning, delete individual learned records or a complete topic bank, clear learned categories and configure which apps/projects/categories may contribute where supported. Disabling learning stops creation/reinforcement of new learned state but MUST NOT silently delete existing Persistent Memory or unrelated user data.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Persistent Memory and Background Learning are independent. Persistent Memory stores durable cross-session memories under the Memory policy; Background Learning is the opt-in process that derives usage patterns, interests, Knowledge Banks and other personalisation state. Neither feature may silently enable, disable, clear or substitute for the other.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Background Learning may identify information that would be useful as a durable memory, but any conversion into Persistent Memory must use the Memory subsystem and preserve that the source was an inference rather than an explicit user statement. Explicit Memory corrections remain authoritative over contradictory Background Learning inferences.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Background Learning is off until the user opts in and remains independently configurable from Persistent Memory.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Eligible 9to1 usage/project patterns, interests/Knowledge Banks and other useful personalisation information can be learned as structured, inspectable state.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Topic Knowledge Banks can provide relevant offline reference material and retain provenance/freshness sufficient to avoid presenting stale inferred facts as timeless truth.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Only relevant learning context is retrieved for a request; the full learning store is not injected indiscriminately.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Learned data is not sold, used for advertising profiles or uploaded to cloud providers merely because learning is enabled.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Users can inspect, correct, scope and delete learning independently of Persistent Memory.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_3
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Plugins and web integrations — WebMCP and site-hosted MCP servers

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_2
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Connect once, reuse through authorised capabilities

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_2
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Live, cached, imported and synchronised state

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: 9to1-OS is derived from the latest appropriate maintained Ubuntu/GNOME stack. The project forks/adapts the complete relevant desktop/system stack rather than treating Ubuntu merely as a kernel image, then rebuilds the 9to1 user-facing desktop environment and first-party system interfaces in CUI.NET while preserving mature non-replaced functionality underneath.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The governing donor rule is preserve unless replaced: applicable Ubuntu/GNOME behaviour, hardware support, accessibility, session management, networking, Bluetooth, audio, displays, power, notifications, multi-monitor support, virtual desktops, filesystem/system integration and other mature platform behaviour MUST remain available unless this specification explicitly replaces or supersedes it.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Where 9to1 requires a CUI.NET replacement for functionality already supplied by Ubuntu/GNOME and that 9to1 product does not already have a different authoritative donor, the latest appropriate corresponding Ubuntu/GNOME application becomes its donor. The replacement preserves applicable donor functionality and rebuilds/extends its GUI in CUI.NET. Existing explicitly assigned donors take precedence; Files, for example, retains its existing donor rather than switching to the Ubuntu file manager.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Once an authoritative 9to1 app fully replaces a donor graphical application, the duplicate donor user-facing app SHOULD be removed from the default OS image. Required lower-level libraries/services remain installed where technically necessary. The objective is functional preservation without parallel competing GUIs.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_1
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Desktop shell and Windows-style interaction model

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The default 9to1-OS shell uses a familiar Windows-like desktop interaction model while retaining Linux/Ubuntu capabilities. Conventional minimise, maximise/restore and close controls, taskbar representation, window switching, context menus, system tray/status, desktop workspaces and predictable mouse/keyboard behaviour are first-class rather than hidden or intentionally omitted.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Drag windows to edges/corners to preview and snap them into supported layouts.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Support built-in and user-defined snap layouts, including half, thirds, quarters and custom rectangular regions with configurable gaps/margins.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Provide smooth configurable window movement, open/close, minimise/restore, maximise, snapping and desktop-transition animations, with reduced-motion/disabled options.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Support conventional app/window switching, previews, multiple windows per app, virtual-desktop awareness, task-view/overview and keyboard-first operation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Support user-configurable per-app/window rules such as initial monitor, desktop, size, snap region, maximised/fullscreen and always-on-top where compatible.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Linux/GTK/Qt and other compatible desktop applications remain runnable even when they are not CUI-native. They participate in the taskbar, window switching, snapping, desktops and supported system integration to the extent the underlying platform permits.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The taskbar is a first-class highly customisable shell framework, not a fixed strip of running applications. The default layout places Go at the left/start position and system/status controls toward the end, but supported regions/items can be rearranged.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Users can configure edge/position, floating versus edge-attached presentation, width, thickness, margins, corner radius, padding, item spacing, alignment, opacity, blur/material, borders, shadows, icon size, labels, grouping/combining, auto-hide/intelligent hide, animations, per-monitor behaviour, clock/tray content and compatible multi-row or multiple-taskbar arrangements.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A taskbar instance supports between one and five independently configurable Taskbar Layers. Scrolling or a configured vertical gesture while the pointer/focus is over the taskbar moves discretely between adjacent layers and snaps to a complete layer; layers are not an infinitely scrollable strip.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Every layer has stable identity, name/order, item layout, presentation and visibility settings. Layers may differ in item size, alignment, grouping, height and visual presentation where supported. A visible accessible layer-position indicator shows the current position and number of available layers; its presentation can be configured but must not rely on colour alone.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A layer can contain typed items such as pinned/running apps, individual windows, Go, system controls, quick actions, settings, files/folders, Shelf items/collections, 9to1 routes, Dulche Agents, Agent runs, Automations actions, widgets, status indicators, media controls, spacers and authorised extension-provided modules.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Examples are illustrative rather than hard-coded: one user may create Running Apps, Quick Actions, AI Agents, Development and Personal layers. No layer type is reserved to a specific category.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_1
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Desktop Spaces, Virtual Desktops and Desktop Pages

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The OS-level mode system is named Desktop Spaces. The existing conversational/AI product is named LLM Spaces. Documentation, APIs and UI MUST use these distinct names to avoid ambiguity.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Virtual Desktops organise sets of windows within the current shell experience. Desktop Spaces redefine the surrounding shell/interaction experience. Desktop Pages are multiple pages of desktop icons/widgets within a desktop surface. These are separate orthogonal concepts.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A Desktop Space is a versioned shell/behaviour profile that may change taskbars, taskbar layers, Go layout, quick settings, notification presentation, window rules, widgets/overlays, input model, theme, animations, performance/resource profile, default actions and Dulche behaviour without requiring applications to restart where avoidable.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: First-party examples include a Gaming Desktop Space that can replace the standard taskbar with a lightweight floating gaming pill showing configurable telemetry such as FPS/frame time, CPU/GPU/RAM/VRAM, temperature, battery/power and latency, with an expandable quick menu; and a Touch Desktop Space that increases targets/spacing and adapts window controls, Go, quick settings, gestures, keyboard integration and snapping for tablet use.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Users can create, duplicate, rename, reorder, import/export, sync and delete custom Desktop Spaces. Optional triggers may suggest or activate a Desktop Space based on convertible posture, controller connection, application launch, display configuration, schedule or other supported state; automatic activation behaviour is user-controlled.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Virtual Desktops support create/delete, names, ordering, keyboard/touchpad switching, window movement between desktops, configurable transition, task-view overview, optional per-desktop wallpaper and configurable taskbar visibility across current/all desktops.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Each desktop surface can contain multiple ordered Desktop Pages that users may add/remove, rename, reorder and navigate by configured gesture/scroll. Pages may contain icons, files/folders, Shelf collections, shortcuts and native CUI widgets and may be global or Desktop-Space-specific according to configuration.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Desktop widgets are first-class CUI entities with resizing, grid/free placement where enabled, ordering, transparency/background material, interaction, update policy and per-page/per-Desktop-Space presence. First-party apps can expose widgets such as Planner, Maps, Files folders, Shelf collections, media, system resources, battery, clock/calendar, quick actions, Dulche Agents and Agent-run state.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Customisation is an architectural property of 9to1-OS. The requirement is not satisfied by wallpaper, accent colour and taskbar-position options. Stable shell behaviour and presentation that can reasonably be represented as configuration SHOULD be configurable unless doing so would materially compromise security, accessibility, compatibility or system integrity.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The OS MUST expose substantially deeper supported first-party customisation than stock Windows or stock GNOME without requiring registry hacks, shell patches, unsupported extensions or third-party Start/taskbar replacements. Configuration uses versioned typed schemas and transactions so Settings, Dulche, Automations and authorised extensions operate on the same underlying state.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Applicable settings can be scoped globally, per device, display, Desktop Space, Virtual Desktop, application/window class or input mode. The implementation MUST define deterministic precedence so a Desktop-Space/display/app override cannot unpredictably conflict with global defaults. Device/display-specific state must not be blindly synced to incompatible hardware.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Mouse pointer/cursor theme, colour, size, outline/high-visibility behaviour and supported custom pointer packs.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Window button order/side, visible controls, button size/spacing/shape, title alignment, titlebar height, icon/title visibility and compatible extra window actions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Window corner roundness, borders, shadows, glow, transparency, active/inactive treatment and user-selectable numerical/preset radius where supported.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Theme profiles covering light/dark/automatic mode, colours, gradients, accents, glow, blur, transparency, shadows, borders, roundness, spacing/density, typography, icons, control shapes and animation character.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Built-in visual personalities such as clean/minimal, glow, playful, glass/classic or other first-party presets act as editable starting profiles rather than locked themes; users can create custom profiles.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Icon packs, per-app icon overrides, icon scale/shape/treatment and notification-badge presentation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Global and per-category animation enablement, speed, reduced-motion and presets/custom timing.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Rebindable keyboard shortcuts, supported mouse/touchpad/touch/controller gestures and conflict detection.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: System tray/status ordering, visibility policy, overflow, icon size/spacing, clock/date/seconds/time-zone presentation, battery percentage/remaining-time presentation and network/audio/Bluetooth/VPN indicators.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Large shell changes SHOULD support preview/keep/revert flows. Configuration mutations are transactional where practical and the shell maintains last-known-good recovery paths including reset current element, reset taskbar, reset Desktop Space, reset appearance, restore previous configuration and safe/default shell mode.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Configuration schemas are versioned and migrations MUST preserve supported user state across OS updates rather than silently discarding a highly customised desktop.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Quick Settings combines Windows-style desktop system controls with Android-style customisation. Users can add/remove/reorder tiles, choose supported sizes, resize tiles, use multiple pages, configure layout/density/panel placement and install authorised custom tiles.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: First-party tiles should cover relevant controls such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, airplane mode, brightness, volume/audio output, microphone, battery saver/performance mode, night light, accessibility, hotspot, VPN, display/casting, input, focus/do-not-disturb, location, screenshot/recording and Dulche/AI state.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Tiles are typed CUI modules that may expose live state, icon, primary/secondary labels, toggle/action, slider and expanded view. Apps/Plugins may register tiles through a permissioned contract with declared supported sizes/actions; arbitrary shell code injection is not a tile API.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Related flyouts such as audio, network, Bluetooth, calendar, battery and notification centre must provide friendly direct controls and the expected Windows-class QoL, including optional battery percentage, output-device switching, tray overflow, date/calendar, power/session controls and useful status detail.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche is an always-available OS assistant, not merely another application. 'Always available' does not require a large model to remain permanently resident: users control model residency/background behaviour while the lightweight service remains integrated with Go AI mode, shortcuts, voice where enabled, context menus, selections, taskbar layers/widgets, notifications, Settings and first-party apps.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Settings contains first-class AI areas for Models/Universal Model Picker, Dulche service/background behaviour, Always-active AI, Persistent Memory and Memory Frequency, Background Learning, Agents, MCP servers, Skills/Plugins, privacy and resource policy. Built-in MCP management includes add/remove, transport/endpoint configuration, authentication, capability inspection, enable/disable, Agent/app permission assignment, health and logs/errors.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Always-active AI is a configurable service mode and MUST NOT grant blanket access to microphone, files, external services or other sensitive capabilities. Those remain separately permissioned.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The default OS must be aggressively memory-efficient without sacrificing specified functionality or quality so local models can use more of the machine. 9to1-OS should lazy-load non-critical services/surfaces, suspend or trim eligible inactive apps, reclaim caches, use appropriate compression/zram and memory mapping, avoid duplicated runtime state and unload inactive models/compatibility environments when policy permits.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Users can configure a managed System Memory Budget/profile such as Minimum, Balanced, Performance, AI/Maximum model capacity or Custom. This is a target for reclaimable/non-critical OS consumption rather than an unsafe hard cap on kernel/critical services.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: An optional Prioritise AI memory policy may reclaim eligible caches/background apps/models more aggressively to make room for a requested local model. Dulche/runtime should report what can be reclaimed and coordinate with the OS resource manager rather than simply failing at the first memory-pressure condition.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Common useful system-administration operations that Ubuntu frequently exposes primarily through Terminal SHOULD have first-party CUI.NET workflows wherever they can be represented safely and coherently. Terminal remains fully available for advanced/unrestricted workflows, but ordinary maintenance must not require memorising shell commands.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Software/package install, removal, update and repository/source management.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: System updates, recovery, backups/snapshots and repair.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Drivers, devices, displays, audio, networking, DNS, VPN, firewall and hotspot.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Disk/partition/filesystem management, mounts, storage cleanup and health information.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Users/groups, permissions/ownership, startup/background services, scheduled jobs and environment/PATH management where appropriate.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Logs/journal/crash diagnostics, process/resource management and compatibility/runtime management.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Friendly GUIs should call stable typed system services/APIs rather than merely concatenate opaque shell strings. Where a shell tool is the only practical backend, arguments must be structured, privilege requirements declared and output/errors/progress handled safely.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_1
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Terminal safety and privileged destructive operations

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: 9to1 Terminal Command Mode includes a Dangerous Command Guard that parses known commands/arguments/targets and classifies risk rather than relying only on substring matching. Potentially major irreversible operations such as destructive recursive deletion, filesystem formatting, partition-table mutation, mass permission changes or dangerous system/boot-path modification require OS-mediated protection.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: For a Dangerous operation the mandatory sequence is consequence-specific warning -> trusted user authentication -> second consequence-specific confirmation -> execution. Authentication is never treated as final consent. The warning should identify resolved targets and expected consequence where feasible.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Terminal AI Mode, Dulche, Agents, Plugins and Automations cannot type the password, approve their own warning or bypass the final confirmation. Script/program execution cannot be perfectly predicted; recognised dangerous privileged operations should still pass through the system safety broker where technically possible, without claiming semantic proof over arbitrary executable code.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: 9to1-OS supports multiple isolated user accounts/profiles with standard and administrator roles, secure per-user data/settings/secrets, fast switching/sign-out and clearly scoped system-wide versus user-specific configuration.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Administrators can create managed policy profiles for family, school, organisation or kiosk-style deployments. Policies can control application allow/deny lists, package/app installation, external providers, Plugins/MCP, Terminal/admin access, removable storage, networking/VPN, Desktop Space/customisation options, web/content controls where supported, update policy and other security-sensitive capabilities.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A School profile can, for example, block launching unapproved applications and prevent the restricted user from disabling that policy without administrator authentication. Enforcement MUST occur below the normal app UI so renaming a binary, launching through Go/Terminal/Shelf or invoking an Agent does not trivially bypass policy.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Managed restrictions must be visible and attributable ('Managed by administrator/school policy') rather than presented as broken UI. Administrators require auditability of policy changes and clear recovery controls; administration must not silently expose another user's private content unless an explicit policy/capability legitimately grants that access.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_1
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: First-party apps and deep OS integration

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: All release-scope first-party 9to1 applications are installed by default as part of the complete 9to1-OS experience, while application updates are independently deliverable from full OS updates. A central update/package service handles discovery, automatic/manual updates, integrity checks, history, repair and supported rollback instead of every app shipping a private updater.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: First-party apps MUST behave as native OS components and register applicable typed integration with Go, Automations, Dulche, notifications, taskbar/layers, Desktop Spaces, widgets, system search/indexing, Files/open-with/default apps, share/clipboard/drag-drop, URI routes, permissions, External App Integrations, background tasks, crash/System Log, updates, backup/recovery, theming/accessibility and resource management.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Automations is a particularly strong integration requirement: apps should expose supported typed triggers/actions/events through the shared Automation framework rather than implementing incompatible private automation engines.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: First-party apps should expose lifecycle information allowing safe trim/suspend/resume under memory pressure without losing unsaved work. Desktop Spaces own shell layout/presentation; apps contribute declared widgets/actions/status rather than taking arbitrary control of the shell.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: 9to1-OS MUST provide a friendly graphical CUI.NET installer and first-run/OOBE experience. A normal installation MUST NOT require interacting with the traditional Linux text/terminal installer or memorising shell commands. Advanced/technical options may be exposed through expandable UI without making them mandatory for ordinary users.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The setup flow should cover applicable language/region, keyboard, accessibility from the first screen, networking, installation target/disk choices, encryption, timezone, user creation and administrator role, optional managed school/organisation setup, privacy/telemetry choices, update preferences, restore from an existing 9to1 backup/profile, initial appearance/Desktop-Space choices and optional Dulche/model/provider onboarding.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Installation progress is staged and truthful. Failures expose actionable explanation, retry/back navigation where safe, logs/technical details and recovery rather than dropping users into an unexplained terminal. Critical-stage failure MUST NOT be presented as successful installation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: 9to1-OS provides a custom CUI recovery environment designed for ordinary users. It should expose Continue/boot normally, automatic startup repair, restore a previous healthy snapshot, undo the latest system update, safe mode, package/system repair, filesystem/disk checks, disable problematic drivers or shell extensions, recover/reset shell configuration, inspect System Log, backup/restore, advanced Terminal and supported repair/reinstall-with-data-preservation flows.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The custom 9to1 Recovery environment supplements rather than replaces the underlying Ubuntu/Linux recovery environment. The stock/default recovery path MUST remain available as an emergency fallback if the custom CUI recovery environment is damaged or cannot launch.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The custom and stock recovery paths must obey the existing boot-safety contract: ordinary snapshot restore, repair and rollback do not rewrite firmware or bootloader code. Any bootloader/firmware update is a separate tightly guarded operation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A normal user can install, create an account, configure basic hardware/privacy choices and reach the desktop without Terminal.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Accessibility and technical details are available during setup rather than only after installation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: 9to1 Recovery provides friendly repair/rollback tools, while the lower-level Ubuntu/Linux recovery environment remains independently reachable.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Installer/recovery failures preserve diagnostic information and do not falsely report success or silently perform bootloader/firmware rewrites.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: System maintenance has a first-party CUI Settings workflow for checking, downloading, scheduling and installing OS updates, viewing changelogs/details, restart requirements, progress, failure/retry and update history. Terminal/package-manager commands remain optional advanced interfaces, never the required normal update path.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Consequential system updates use verified recoverable system snapshots/rollback state where technically feasible. The system should confirm successful boot/health before retiring rollback state and provide a friendly recovery environment with restore previous snapshot, repair OS/package database, safe mode, diagnostic logs and extension/driver disablement.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Ordinary backup/snapshot restoration and update rollback MUST NOT overwrite or restore firmware or bootloader code as part of the rollback transaction. Bootloader/firmware updates, if ever necessary, are separate tightly guarded operations with their own compatibility/recovery process so a normal failed OS update is not turned into a bricked device.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: 9to1-OS includes a friendly CUI graphical package manager with search, categories, source/publisher, version, architecture, size, installed/update state, screenshots/metadata where available, dependency/permission information and install/update/uninstall/repair workflows.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The package manager uses typed PackageProvider adapters for applicable Linux package ecosystems such as Ubuntu/Debian packages, Flatpak, Snap if retained and coherent AppImage handling, plus Winget for supported Windows/Wine scenarios and 9to1 package sources. It may show multiple sources for the same product and explain meaningful differences instead of silently choosing an arbitrary provider.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: PackageProvider contracts define search, metadata, versions, install/update/uninstall, dependencies, progress, source trust, errors and capability limitations so additional providers can integrate without rewriting the package-manager UI.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: 9to1-OS includes a CUI System Log surface that translates underlying journal/service/app events into useful searchable/filterable diagnostics while retaining advanced technical detail. Events can expose timestamp, component/process, severity, subsystem, version/build, crash ID, stack/debug data where available and related logs/actions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Crash records should group repeated failures, support export/diagnostic bundles and permit user-authorised Dulche analysis such as explaining why a component repeatedly crashed. Diagnostic information MUST NOT be silently uploaded.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Settings includes CUI Disk Management covering physical disks, partitions, filesystems, mounts, labels, free/used space, removable storage, format/partition operations, encryption state, filesystem checks and SMART/health data where supported. Destructive operations require clear device identification and appropriate confirmation/authentication.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: HEADING_2
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Task Manager and other donor-backed utilities

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Task Manager is rebuilt in CUI.NET using the appropriate Ubuntu/GNOME system-monitor tooling as donor baseline unless another donor is explicitly assigned. It preserves mature process/resource functionality and extends it with Windows-style usability plus 9to1-specific visibility for models, Agents, containers/compatibility environments and relevant GPU/RAM usage.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The same donor fallback rule applies to Settings and other required CUI system utilities when an appropriate Ubuntu/GNOME app exists and no different donor has already been assigned.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Ubuntu/GNOME mature non-replaced functionality is preserved while the authoritative user-facing shell/system GUIs are CUI.NET and duplicate replaced donor apps are removed from the default image.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The taskbar is deeply customisable and supports one to five discrete snapping layers with a visible accessible layer indicator.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Desktop Spaces, Virtual Desktops, Desktop Pages and LLM Spaces remain explicitly separate concepts.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The shell supports deep first-party customisation of taskbar, Go, Quick Settings, pointer, window chrome/roundness, themes, widgets, desktops, gestures, tray/status, animations and scoped per-device/display/Desktop-Space/app behaviour.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Dulche, MCP, models and AI-aware memory/resource controls are first-class OS settings and Dulche is always available without requiring a heavyweight model to remain loaded.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Common administration has friendly CUI workflows and Dangerous Terminal operations use warning -> authentication -> final confirmation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Multiple users and enforceable administrator-managed profiles can restrict unapproved apps and other capabilities without trivial bypass through alternate launch surfaces.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: All first-party 9to1 apps ship installed by default, update independently and integrate deeply with shared OS services including Automations.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: System updates have GUI installation, verified recovery/rollback mechanisms and ordinary rollback does not rewrite firmware/bootloader code.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A friendly multi-provider package manager, System Log/crash diagnostics, Disk Management and donor-backed Task Manager/Settings are present as first-class CUI system utilities.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Go is the universal Start/search/action surface for 9to1-OS. It combines the roles of a Windows-style Start menu, system-wide search, application launcher and contextual quick-action surface. Go is an OS primitive, not a separate heavyweight application, and the default taskbar places Go at the left/start position.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Opening Go without a query presents a customisable home surface that can contain Pinned items, Recent items, Suggested/contextual items, All Apps, recent files/projects, quick system actions, account/session controls and power controls. Users can reorder, hide, resize or regroup supported sections and choose compact search-first, Start-menu-like or larger dashboard-oriented layouts.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: All Apps is a first-class Go view containing installed applications/programs available to the current user/profile. It is separate from the Android-style Launcher app drawer. Go is the primary application-launcher replacement for the 9to1-OS desktop shell.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Go provides a Search / AI switcher. Search is deterministic universal search/navigation; AI routes natural-language intent through Dulche while using the same canonical Go providers and typed OS/app actions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Examples of AI-mode requests include opening the project the user was working on, finding the setting that controls display scaling, launching a group of development tools or locating notes by context. AI mode MUST NOT fabricate applications, files, settings or entities that do not exist and MUST surface ambiguity when multiple plausible targets remain.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Applications, frameworks and authorised extensions register typed GoProviders rather than requiring Go to hard-code product-specific databases.
