Providers may expose search, suggestions, recent items, result categories, previews, aliases, quick actions, indexing/change notifications and query-time-only results.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Go may search applications, files/folders, settings, people/contacts, LLM Spaces/conversations where authorised, Boards, Planner tasks/events, Maps places, Shelf items/collections, Stack repositories/branches, Dev projects, browser history/bookmarks where enabled, installed tools, Plugins/extensions and registered system actions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Go returns references to canonical entities owned by their source application/framework. Its local index may cache identifiers, search fields, aliases, presentation metadata, permissions and freshness state, but MUST NOT create a competing canonical copy of a file, document, project, place, person or other result merely because it is searchable.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Ranking may combine exact/prefix/fuzzy match, aliases, keywords, recency, frequency, pins/favourites, current app, active project, current canonical object, Desktop Space, user-enabled Background Learning and provider relevance. Context can change ranking and available actions but never bypass access controls or change the canonical identity of a result.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Results can expose owner-provided typed actions such as Open, Reveal, Share, Navigate, New window, Pin, Create, Toggle, Open with or app-specific commands. Go may invoke these actions directly where appropriate but MUST NOT reproduce another app's private business logic.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Consequential actions remain subject to the underlying OS/app permission and confirmation requirements. Go and Dulche cannot use a quick-action surface to bypass security prompts.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Go supports optional user-selectable filters/categories such as Apps, Files, People, Settings, Places, Projects and Actions plus provider-defined categories where useful. Results may expose compact CUI previews supplied from canonical provider data.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Providers declare whether they are locally indexed, queried live or hybrid. They can push changed entities, invalidate deleted entities and request re-indexing. Search results MUST be permission-filtered before display, including for restricted folders/projects, managed user profiles and lock-screen contexts.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Users can disable sensitive providers/categories such as browser history, message contents or private project indexing. Stale/offline remote results must be marked with their freshness state and invalid/deleted results removed rather than accumulating as zombie entries.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The same Go framework may be embedded as a scoped picker/search surface in Launcher, Files, Shelf and other apps, and Dulche may query Go for authorised entity discovery. These are scoped views over the same provider contracts, not separate incompatible search engines.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Opening Go should be effectively immediate. Local providers should stream results incrementally; slow remote providers MUST NOT block applications, local files, settings or cached results. Failure of one provider is isolated and reported only for that provider.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Go acts as the primary 9to1-OS Start menu, universal search and quick-action surface, with Go at the default left/start taskbar position.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Pinned, Recent, Suggested and All Apps views are first-class and deeply customisable.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Search and AI modes use the same canonical entity/provider/action contracts; AI mode cannot hallucinate unavailable entities.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Search results remain permission-filtered canonical references rather than duplicate Go-owned objects.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Provider failures and remote latency do not block local search/launch functionality.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: On 9to1-OS, the Universal Model Picker is the OS-hosted presentation of the same canonical Dulche/Home model/provider state used by regular 9to1. Model identities, provider connections, ordered Model Routes, active/background routing, category overrides, fallbacks, permissions and usage state MUST remain interoperable across Home and 9to1-OS rather than becoming separate OS-only configuration.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The OS picker provides the same compact selection experience plus deeper integration with Settings → AI, system resource management, administrator policy and local-model lifecycle. It can expose local/cloud/remote identity, capabilities, reasoning/effort controls, aliases/nicknames, route order, fallback state, locality/privacy, loading/residency, RAM/VRAM fit and per-app/Agent/Desktop-Space overrides.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: 9to1-OS may host the picker natively while Windows regular 9to1 hosts it through Home, but both clients MUST read/write the same versioned routing contracts and Dulche model catalogue. A route configured in Home remains meaningful on 9to1-OS subject to device-local model availability, provider authentication, administrator policy and device-specific resource constraints.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: When a selected local model requires additional memory, the picker integrates with the 9to1-OS resource broker to show required/available/reclaimable RAM/VRAM and may request permitted reclamation before declaring the model unavailable. It MUST distinguish Installed, Unloaded, Loading, Loaded, Offloaded/Partially loaded where supported and Unavailable due to resources.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Administrator-managed user profiles can restrict allowed models/providers, cloud use, model acquisition and routing fallback. Model ordering MUST never bypass those restrictions; policy-ineligible candidates are filtered before route selection.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Ordered model fallback is a shared 9to1 capability, not an OS-specific behaviour. Requests from regular 9to1/Home and 9to1-OS use the same eligibility-first routing semantics: determine required capabilities and policy constraints, filter the configured route, then choose the highest-priority eligible available model and fall through only on classified model/provider-routing conditions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The Wine/WinBoat Framework is the unified 9to1-OS compatibility platform for non-native application packages. It provides one coherent installation, routing, execution, lifecycle, permissions, diagnostics and shell-integration model across Windows applications and Android APK applications rather than exposing Wine, VM/container tooling or an Android runtime as unrelated expert-only subsystems.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A CompatibilityBackend is a typed implementation capable of installing/running one or more foreign application formats. Required backend classes include a Wine-compatible Windows runtime, a WinBoat-style Windows environment for applications needing a fuller Windows VM/container context, and an APK/Android compatibility layer for Android applications. Additional compatible backends MAY be registered later through the same framework.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The compatibility manager owns stable entities such as CompatibilityApp, CompatibilityPackage, CompatibilityBackend, CompatibilityEnvironment, CompatibilityRoute, AppRoutingRule, CompatibilityPermissionSet, CompatibilityHealth and CompatibilitySnapshot or equivalent contracts. Applications are identified by stable package/application identity rather than by the pathname of the installer that originally created them.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Opening or double-clicking a supported foreign application package MUST route through the compatibility framework automatically. Executable/package type should be determined from trusted file metadata/signature/MIME inspection where available rather than relying only on filename extension.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Windows .exe/.msi and equivalent supported installers are routed to an eligible Windows backend. Android .apk packages are routed to an eligible APK/Android compatibility backend. The normal user experience is Install/Open application, not manually invoking wine, configuring a prefix, running Docker/Podman/QEMU/RDP commands or issuing Android runtime commands in Terminal.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The router evaluates package type, known application identity, architecture, backend capability, existing environments, administrator policy, resource requirements, compatibility knowledge and user defaults. When there is one clear eligible default, routing should proceed without unnecessary questions. When multiple viable frameworks exist or the user requests control, the UI may ask which framework/backend to use.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Users can set a preferred/default CompatibilityBackend for each installed application or recognised application identity. A chooser can provide an explicit 'Always use this framework for this app' action. This preference is stored against stable app/package identity and survives moves/renames of the original installer.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: A per-app default does not override hard incompatibility, missing backend capability, administrator policy or unavailable hardware. If the selected backend cannot satisfy the app, the framework reports why and may offer other eligible backends rather than silently executing through an unrelated path.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Users can change/reset the backend association later from the application's compatibility settings. Global defaults may exist for Windows packages and APK packages, but per-app rules take precedence where valid.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The Wine backend manages Wine runtime/version, isolated prefixes/environments, application architecture, DLL/runtime dependencies, graphics/DirectX translation, environment variables, registry integration, drive mappings, fonts, file associations, launch arguments and per-app overrides through CUI.NET management surfaces.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Ordinary users MUST NOT need to manually run winecfg, winetricks, edit registry state or construct WINEPREFIX environment variables. Advanced views may expose equivalent controls and raw technical details when useful.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Applications SHOULD normally use isolated managed Wine environments so dependency/runtime changes, repair, backup and uninstall do not corrupt unrelated apps. Applications may deliberately share an environment when required, but that relationship must be explicit.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The WinBoat-style backend provides a managed Windows VM/container environment for applications that need or work better with a fuller Windows installation. It may expose configurable CPU, RAM, storage, hardware acceleration, networking, shared folders, USB/device passthrough, graphics configuration and individual-app/RemoteApp-style window integration where supported.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The management experience hides Docker/Podman, QEMU, VM orchestration and RDP implementation details during normal use while retaining advanced diagnostics. Individual Windows applications should appear as normal 9to1-OS windows where technically possible; a full Windows desktop remains available as a fallback/advanced mode.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: 9to1-OS MUST support Android APK applications through the same Compatibility Framework using an Android/APK compatibility layer. Installing an APK creates/registers a normal CompatibilityApp backed by the Android runtime rather than placing Android apps in a disconnected secondary launcher.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The APK backend is responsible for Android runtime/container lifecycle, package installation/update/removal, Android package identity, architecture/ABI compatibility, graphics acceleration, display/window integration, storage mappings, networking, clipboard, audio, microphone/camera, notifications, input, orientation, intents/file associations and other host bridges where supported.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Android applications should participate in Go, taskbar/taskbar layers, window switching, Desktop Spaces, notifications, Files/open-with/share flows, Shelf and other applicable 9to1-OS integrations. The Android compatibility layer MUST NOT require the user to launch a separate Android desktop merely to start an installed APK unless a full Android environment is explicitly requested.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: If multiple APK-compatible runtimes/backends are available, the same automatic eligibility and per-app default framework rules apply. The user may choose a backend and persist it for that Android app; otherwise 9to1 selects the highest-priority eligible configured default.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Opening a supported .exe, .msi, .apk or other registered foreign package invokes a single compatibility installation flow showing detected application/package identity, recommended backend, destination environment, required permissions, storage/resource estimate and relevant compatibility warnings. Advanced settings expose backend-specific controls without requiring them for a normal install.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The GUI package manager may also install Windows software through Winget or other approved Windows sources and Android packages through approved configured package sources where supported. Package-source discovery does not bypass administrator policy, signing/trust requirements or compatibility permissions.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Foreign applications remain subject to the same shell/platform integration expectations as native applications wherever technically possible: Go search/launch, taskbar and layers, Desktop Spaces, snapping, app switching, tray/status integration, Files/open-with, default associations, clipboard, drag/drop, audio/microphone, printing, notifications, shortcuts, recent items, System Log/crash diagnostics and resource management.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Compatibility apps may expose Automations/Dulche actions only through typed supported bridges. Running inside Wine, a Windows VM or an Android runtime does not give an application unrestricted access to the host Automation framework or other 9to1 capabilities.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Host folder exposure is explicit and revocable. Compatibility environments receive only user/admin-authorised Files locations rather than unrestricted access to the entire Linux home directory by default. Shared-folder mappings identify the canonical host location and the guest-visible mapping.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Clipboard, microphone, camera, USB/devices, network modes, location and other sensitive bridges use the normal 9to1 permission/policy system where applicable. A locally running foreign application is not automatically trusted with unrestricted host resources.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The framework exposes backend-appropriate GPU acceleration, Vulkan/DirectX translation, discrete/integrated GPU preference, fullscreen, controller/input support and relevant compatibility/performance settings. Windows or Android games can integrate with Gaming Desktop Space telemetry/controls where the backend exposes the required data.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: CompatibilityEnvironment lifecycle states include at least Starting, Running, Suspended, Stopped, Degraded/Error and backend-specific transitional states. The framework reports allocated and actual RAM/CPU/storage/GPU usage where available and participates in 9to1-OS memory/resource policy so idle VM/container environments can be suspended or stopped according to user policy.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Compatibility environments must preserve application/user state safely across suspend/resume and OS memory pressure. The OS MUST NOT simply terminate a managed environment and discard unsaved guest/application state to satisfy a memory target.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Backends supporting snapshots/checkpoints should expose them through the unified manager, particularly before major guest/runtime changes. Compatibility snapshots are separate from 9to1-OS system snapshots.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The framework manages or coordinates updates for Wine/runtime components, WinBoat-derived host integration, Android compatibility/runtime components and guest-integration tooling. Guest Windows/Android update behaviour remains explicit and must not be confused with host OS updates.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Repair/reset operations should be scoped to the selected app/environment and preserve unrelated environments. Destructive reset/uninstall flows explain whether app data, shared environment state or snapshots will be removed.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The CUI compatibility manager normalises common failures such as missing Wine dependency, application crash, graphics translation failure, Windows guest boot failure, RemoteApp disconnection, Android runtime failure, incompatible APK ABI, insufficient RAM, unavailable hardware acceleration, broken shared folder or package-install failure into actionable health states.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Advanced diagnostics expose underlying Wine/runtime/VM/RDP/Android logs and environment details through System Log integration. Dulche may analyse these diagnostics and invoke typed repair/configuration APIs but should not replace a supported manager operation with arbitrary host shell automation.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Administrator policies can disable foreign-app compatibility entirely, restrict allowed backends, block arbitrary .exe/.msi/.apk installation, allowlist approved applications/package identities, restrict package sources such as Winget/Android sources, constrain host-folder/device/network bridges and lock per-app backend choices.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Launching through Go, Files, Shelf, Terminal, Dulche or another app MUST NOT bypass the same compatibility policy. Policy enforcement occurs in the routing/install/execution broker below the launch surface.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Double-clicking/opening a supported Windows installer/executable or Android APK automatically enters the unified compatibility routing flow rather than requiring Terminal.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Wine, WinBoat-style Windows environments and APK/Android compatibility are represented as typed backends under one manager.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: The user may choose among eligible frameworks and can persist a default framework per application; valid per-app defaults are remembered and editable.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Installed Windows and Android applications integrate with Go, taskbar/window management, Desktop Spaces, Files, notifications, diagnostics and resource policy wherever technically possible.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Host files/devices and sensitive bridges remain explicit permission boundaries, not blanket compatibility-environment access.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Administrator policy applies regardless of which launch surface or compatibility backend is used.

unrepresented_source_paragraphs.heading: NORMAL_TEXT
unrepresented_source_paragraphs.text: Backend-specific complexity remains available for advanced users but is not required for ordinary installation, launch, repair or troubleshooting.
